normative. The outer `J0` is never repeated, and the query-only duplicate is
never placed in an attribute list. `job_list_sha256` is the SHA-256 of one
compact strict-ASCII JSON array of the ordered actual explicit logical IDs plus
exactly one LF. Nested-job support, every suspended membership query, and every
atomic list assignment must succeed; later `AssignProcessToJobObject` is
forbidden.

All owned Jobs are non-inheritable, configured while empty with
`JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, and have no breakaway flag. An owner
retains `JOB_OBJECT_ASSIGN_PROCESS | JOB_OBJECT_SET_ATTRIBUTES |
JOB_OBJECT_QUERY | JOB_OBJECT_TERMINATE`; the root receives only a duplicate of
`J0` with `JOB_OBJECT_QUERY`, clears its inherit flag before any descendant
construction, and closes it at root shutdown. Associate only `J0`, `L0`, and
`J1` with completion ports before their first member. Inner `T`, `Ln`, and
`Cn` Jobs remain unassociated: their members are observed through enclosing
`J1`/`J0` and authoritatively queried directly. Owners close inner Jobs
leaf-first, then `J1`/`J0`, and the applicable completion port last.

If the operator host is itself in an external containing Job, that ambient
ancestor is inherited implicitly, remains unowned, and is excluded from all
Campaign IDs and list digests. The host records only
`ambient_ancestor_job_present`, never attempts breakaway, and treats the
ordered `effective_campaign_job_ids` above as the Campaign-owned suffix.

Inherited handle manifests are exact. A root-broker receives only descriptor-
read, ACK/status-write, GO-read, deterministic stdin-read, stdout-write,
stderr-write, the query-only `outer_job_query`, plus explicitly descriptor-
bound multiprocessing objects for that closed root role. A guarded target
receives descriptor-read, ACK/status-write, GO-read, persistent broker-request-
write, persistent broker-response-read, stdin-read, stdout-write, stderr-write,
plus its explicitly bound multiprocessing objects. A native leaf and a Codex
client root each receive only deterministic stdin/stdout/stderr handles.
Duplicates, pseudo handles, sockets, wrong direction/object type/access, and
any additional inheritable handle reject before construction.

Both authenticated constructor implementations are required by tests to
implement the same exact
`complete-suite-native-constructor-state-machine-v1`. That invariant is bound
by their two authenticated implementation bodies and the constructor-class
registry; it is not an undeclared field in the two-record implementation-set
JSON.

Each supervisor creates exactly one private I/O completion port with
`CreateIoCompletionPort(INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, NULL, 0, 1)`. Completion key `1`
denotes that supervisor's associated `J0`, `L0`, or `J1`; key
`0x1000 + pipe_ordinal` denotes one pipe role. Raw key values are runtime-only,
while durable records bind the typed Job or pipe ordinal. Inner `T`, `Ln`, and
`Cn` Jobs are not associated with another port and are queried directly.

Every applicable internal channel is a distinct local named byte pipe with
grammar `\\.\pipe\kokoroarc-c6-control-<32 lowercase hex>-<fixed-role>`, where
the fixed role is one of `descriptor`, `ack-status`, `go`, `broker-request`,
`broker-response`, `stdin`, `stdout`, or `stderr`. Directions are exact:

| parent action | channel roles | server open mode | child access |
|---|---|---|---|
| writes | `descriptor`, `go`, `broker-response`, `stdin` | `PIPE_ACCESS_OUTBOUND` | `GENERIC_READ` |
| reads | `ack-status`, `broker-request`, `stdout`, `stderr` | `PIPE_ACCESS_INBOUND` | `GENERIC_WRITE` |

For each applicable channel, the constructor performs this exact ordering:

1. Create the non-inheritable server with
   `FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, byte/wait/reject-
   remote modes, one instance, 65,536-byte input/output buffers, and a security
   descriptor granting access only to the current user SID.
2. Associate the server endpoint with the private completion port.
3. Call overlapped `ConnectNamedPipe` before opening the client endpoint. In
   this controlled ordering the only accepted initial result is
   `FALSE/ERROR_IO_PENDING`; `TRUE`, `ERROR_PIPE_CONNECTED`, or any other
   result is an invariant failure.
4. Open the inheritable synchronous child endpoint with `CreateFileW`, its
   table-fixed complementary access, share mode zero, and `OPEN_EXISTING`.
5. Dequeue and validate that pipe's one successful connect completion before
   process creation; its connect `OVERLAPPED` and buffer remain allocated until
   that packet is consumed.
6. Put only the child endpoint in `HANDLE_LIST`. Close the parent's duplicate
   of it immediately after successful `CreateProcessW`.

Each parent endpoint permits exactly one outstanding operation and one
dedicated `OVERLAPPED`; neither that object nor its buffer is reused, moved, or
freed before exact retirement. The one IOCP-owner thread both issues operations
and dequeues their packets, so no other thread may dequeue during an API call.
Immediately before every overlapped `ReadFile` or `WriteFile`, it zeroes the
`OVERLAPPED`, allocates the immutable operation buffer/cursor, and inserts an
`ISSUING` ledger entry. The return transition is exhaustive:

| API return | exact transition |
|---|---|
| `TRUE` | `ISSUING -> LIVE_AWAIT_PACKET`; because completion-skip modes are forbidden, ignore the immediate byte count and retire only from the exact queued packet |
| `FALSE/ERROR_IO_PENDING` | `ISSUING -> LIVE_AWAIT_PACKET`; retire only from the exact queued packet |
| `FALSE/ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE` on a role-permitted read terminal | record immediate EOF, remove `ISSUING`, never mark live, and expect no packet |
| any other `FALSE/GetLastError()` | record the immediate terminal error, remove `ISSUING`, never mark live, and expect no packet |

Only `LIVE_AWAIT_PACKET` is outstanding or cancelable. A successful partial
write advances an immutable cursor and issues a new operation only after the
prior packet retires; a successful zero-byte write is failure. A dequeued read
`ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE` is EOF only at a role-permitted protocol terminal.

All wire caps are constructor-table facts. Define
`F(payload_cap, frames) = frames * (4 + payload_cap)`, where every four-byte
length prefix counts. The exact endpoint caps are:

| role/context | `byte_cap` |
|---|---:|
| descriptor | `F(4194304, 1)` |
| execute-root ACK/status | `F(65536, 4)` |
| every other root or guarded-target ACK/status | `F(65536, 2)` |
| GO | `F(65536, 1)` |
| broker request, per target | `F(65536, 1024)` |
| broker response, per target | `F(65536, 1024)` |
| root broker-request aggregate, across all targets | `F(65536, 4096)` |
| root broker-response aggregate, across all targets | `F(65536, 4096)` |
| credential data | `4 + 65536` |
| credential host status | `F(65536, 1)` |
| raw stdin/stdout/stderr | the exact selected process-limit row's corresponding cap |

The two aggregate broker caps are separate monotonically increasing counters in
addition to every endpoint cap. Before every read or allocation,
`remaining_cap = byte_cap - completed_wire_bytes`; reads request at most
`min(65536, remaining_cap + 1)` so the first over-cap byte is detected but not
retained. A decoded frame length greater than 65,536 or `4 + N` greater than the
remaining cap rejects before payload allocation. Credential-data completed
wire bytes remain ephemeral and are never copied into a durable record; its
fixed cap is not length evidence.

The dispatcher invokes only `GetQueuedCompletionStatus`. A key-`1` Job packet
treats `lpOverlapped` as the documented message value (a PID-sized value where
that message defines one, otherwise null) and never dereferences it; a pipe
packet must match exactly one live `OVERLAPPED`. A false return with non-null
`lpOverlapped` is a dequeued failed I/O completion and is reconciled using its
`GetLastError` value. A false return with null `lpOverlapped` is a poll timeout
only when `GetLastError() == WAIT_TIMEOUT`; every other such result is terminal
dispatcher failure. `SetFileCompletionNotificationModes` is forbidden, so even
an immediately successful overlapped operation retains its allocation until
its completion packet is consumed. Each wait is
`min(50, ceil(remaining_monotonic_ns / 1_000_000))` milliseconds; a nonpositive
remainder is deadline failure without a wait. After every packet or poll
timeout, the owner nonblocking-queries retained process handles and every
applicable Job.

The exact launch sequence is:

1. Create/configure every applicable Job, the completion port, and every pipe,
   and drain all connect completions.
2. Arm the ACK/status, broker-request, stdout, and stderr reads that apply to
   the process class.
3. Call `CreateProcessW` suspended with the exact attribute list and ordered
   `JOB_LIST` described above.
4. Close every parent duplicate of a child endpoint.
5. While the primary thread remains suspended, prove PID/creation time, image,
   OS parent, handle manifest, and membership with `IsProcessInJob` for every
   implicit and explicit Campaign Job. No `NEW_PROCESS` packet is required.
6. Close a zero-cap stdin writer without issuing `WriteFile`; otherwise leave
   it idle until its exact bounded payload is ready.
7. Resume the primary thread exactly once.
8. For a descriptor-gated root or target, write the length-prefixed descriptor
   incrementally and close its writer after the last completion. The child
   authenticates it, observes EOF, and returns one framed ACK. The owner then
   writes one framed GO, closes after its final completion, and requires GO EOF
   before role code. A native leaf or client instead follows only its closed
   stdin/stdout/stderr grammar.
9. Pump the terminal/status, broker, stdio, process, and Job state to the one
   absolute deadline.

Job completion-port notifications are advisory and are not guaranteed by
Windows. `NEW_PROCESS`, exit, and `ACTIVE_PROCESS_ZERO` packets may enrich a
typed, monotonically ordered ledger but are never mandatory success gates.
Success instead requires every retained process handle signaled with a
reconciled exit code; for each owned Job,
`JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation.ActiveProcesses == 0`, an empty final
process-ID list, and `TotalProcesses` equal to the unique known-process count
for that Job scope; all required terminal frames and pipe EOFs; and zero
outstanding I/O. A missed notification that leaves an accounting, identity, or
membership mismatch therefore fails closed.

On any deadline, cap, parser, Job, pipe, process, or ordering failure, the exact
failure sequence is:

1. Atomically freeze new operations.
2. Terminate the smallest owning `Ln`, `Cn`, `T`, `J1`, `L0`, or `J0` Job.
3. Call `CancelIoEx(handle, &overlapped)` for every live operation.
   Success and false/`ERROR_NOT_FOUND` are the only accepted call results;
   neither retires the operation. Only its exact one dequeued completion retires
   it. Success and `ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED` are accepted cleanup completions;
   the independently role-permitted terminal `ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE` EOF is also
   accepted. Every other dequeued completion error still retires that operation
   but remains a terminal protocol failure.
4. Close only idle writers immediately. A writer with pending I/O remains open
   until its success/cancellation completion is consumed.
5. During the single 10,000 ms grace, consume completion packets and poll
   process handles and Job accounting. A canceled stdout/stderr read is not
   recorded as EOF.
6. If all operations retire and every applicable Job is empty, close pipes and
   process handles, then inner Jobs leaf-first, the associated Job, and the
   completion port last.
7. If grace expires, close kill-on-close Jobs, then pipe/process handles, stop
   the pump, and close the completion port last. Quarantine every still-live
   `OVERLAPPED` and buffer until the owning host/root process exits; never
   reuse/free it or publish success.

There is no reconnect, retry, second grace, or handle reuse.

ACK/status, GO, broker-request, and broker-response are four distinct pipe
roles; none aliases another handle or lifetime. Every control frame is exactly
a four-byte unsigned little-endian payload length followed by canonical strict-
UTF-8 JSON, with a 65,536-byte payload cap. A host-facing root ACK/status grammar
is exactly `ack`, then for the `execute` root only zero or one `claim-ready`;
when and only when that readiness frame is followed by an authenticated peer
connection, exactly one `credential-peer-accepted` follows. Then exactly one
`terminal` and EOF follow. Every other root permits only `ack`, then `terminal`,
then EOF. Every target ACK/status grammar is exactly
`ack`, `terminal`, EOF; an execute target sends only the separate secret-free
broker capability defined below, never a target `claim-ready` frame. The GO
grammar is exactly one authenticated `go` frame
followed immediately by writer close and observed EOF. ACK and GO bind protocol
version, descriptor nonce/hash, constructor class/table hash, PID and creation
time. An early/duplicate/reordered/unknown frame, trailing byte, missing EOF,
or close before the required terminal frame fails the whole Job.

The post-capability `credential-data` and `credential-host-status` roles are two
additional distinct, noninherited dynamic roles. They use the same issue ledger,
IOCP dispatch, absolute deadline, cap, cancellation, retirement, and close
rules, but their names, directions, peer authentication, and lifecycle schema
are fixed separately below; neither may alias a constructor control handle.

Each guarded target retains its broker-request writer and broker-response reader
after GO. A request is permitted only after authenticated GO, has a monotonically
increasing sequence beginning at one, and binds protocol version, root and
target descriptor nonce/hash, requested closed role, canonical payload bytes and
payload SHA-256. Exactly one request may be outstanding. Its response repeats
the sequence and descriptor bindings and contains exactly one closed decision,
canonical result payload plus its SHA-256, or a stable public error code. The
target verifies the result bytes before use. The target cap is 1,024 request/
response pairs; the root cap is 4,096 pairs across all targets. At target
shutdown with no outstanding request, it closes the request writer; the root
requires EOF and closes the response writer; the target requires response EOF
before its terminal status frame. No request, response, or descendant may
extend the one continuously decreasing root-role deadline. Frame-cap,
sequence, binding, ordering, count, response, deadline, and EOF drift terminate
the Job and publish no success record.

The broker reserves all pipe ends and buffers but writes no descriptor or role
stdin before process creation. After `CreateProcessW` returns the suspended
member, the parent immediately closes every parent copy of a child-only end,
retains only the exact complementary ends above, verifies Job membership,
PID/creation time, parent, image path/identity/hash, constructor class/table
hash, and handle manifest, then resumes once. It concurrently writes the
descriptor in bounded chunks, closes descriptor and zero-cap stdin writers at
exact EOF, pumps stdout/stderr, status, broker IPC, and Job events, validates
ACK, sends the single GO, and completes all work against the same deadline.
This ordering permits descriptor payloads larger than a named-pipe buffer
without pre-reader deadlock and prevents a retained parent writer from hiding
EOF.

Before any non-stdlib import, the committed root bootstrap validates the
descriptor, nonce, parent PID/creation time, executable/bootstrap locks and
hashes, cwd materialization, constructor class/table hash, handle inventory,
authority/overlays, evaluation envelope, and absence of secret names. It
reconfigures both text streams to the fixed strict UTF-8 contract, installs
filesystem/process/socket/import guards around its broker-only module, emits the
authenticated ACK, then waits for exactly one authenticated GO and its EOF. It
never adds a repository import root. After GO it constructs the one initial
restricted root-role target. That target's bootstrap independently validates
its descriptor/authority/overlays/guards, ACKs, waits for its own GO/EOF, and
only then imports exactly one closed role entrypoint. Every failure closes
handles, terminates the Job, drains without retention under the fixed grace
bound, and publishes no success record. REDs prove a root-broker can construct
only registered closed roles, cannot load a role/repository module, every
guarded target/native leaf is kernel-restricted from direct process creation,
and class/table or dedicated-pipe mutations reject precreation.

The `execute` root is explicitly a trusted `root-broker` and starts without
`OPENAI_API_KEY` in its environment, descriptor, argv, or inherited handles.
Before ACK, the Task 9 stdlib-only pre-ACK validator authenticates the
authorization/reservation bytes and proves the execute marker, terminal, raw
root, and claim absent; it imports no Task 10/repository role and consumes or
claims nothing. The host validates that state and ACK, then sends GO. The fresh
post-GO execute target imports the Task 10 validator, reopens the same authority,
calls `consume_provider_execute` exactly once and `claim_provider_attempt`
exactly once, reopens the frozen client identity, and completes the process-free
`prepare_claimed_campaign` skeleton while both lifecycle paths remain absent. It
then sends one
secret-free `execute-claim-capability` broker request binding its descriptor,
authorization/reservation/marker/claim hashes, raw-root identity, frozen client
identity/spec digest, and target PID/creation time. It cannot create the secret
pipe or receive a credential. The root-broker independently reopens and
revalidates every referenced fact and only then creates the paired first-instance
nonce-bound credential-data and host-status named pipes under the exact protocol
below. After both pipe servers are armed, the root emits the one
authenticated host-facing `claim-ready` frame on its still-open ACK/status
channel, binding root and target descriptor hashes, marker/claim hashes, client
spec digest, transport/name literals, both typed pipe-name records, and authenticated
host, root, and target PID/creation-time identities.

The request wrapper's role is exactly `execute-claim-capability`, its sequence is
the target's next broker sequence, and its canonical payload is exactly
`ExecuteClaimCapability`; no path, credential value, environment mapping,
free-form message, or extra field is permitted. The target sends this request at
most once and blocks with it as the sole outstanding request. The root's
Task 9 stdlib-only `validate_execute_claim_capability_stdlib` reparses the
canonical bytes and independently reopens all descriptor-bound inputs; it does
not import or call Task 10-through-16 code and does not trust the target's
detached validation result. Only exact agreement permits the root to construct
canonical `ExecuteClaimReady` bytes and the pipe. The broker response remains
pending while the host validates that readiness frame and while both pipe peers
complete the identity exchange below. It remains pending while the root
concurrently drains credential data and the separate host-status channel,
validates the status/data join, closes both channels, and constructs the
lifecycle DAG below. Only after that join does the root return the secret-free
decision `execute-root-authority-ready`; otherwise it returns one stable public
error when the joined lifecycle represents an orderly failure. A missing or
invalid post-readiness status produces no ordinary broker response and enters
the consumed-invalid path.
The same closed response wrapper carries exactly null for each of
`credential_pipe_lifecycle`, `credential_pipe_lifecycle_sha256`,
`credential_lifecycle`, and `credential_lifecycle_sha256` before readiness, or
the complete canonical secret-free root-side pipe lifecycle and credential-
lifecycle objects and their hashes after readiness. The root closes both
credential channels before returning either response. A capability request
that fails before readiness is sealable only when the target authenticates the
exact broker response bytes/hash and constructs
`AuthenticatedPreReadinessBrokerFailureTransport`; all four lifecycle
projections remain null. A failure before any capability send instead requires
the execute target's private, single-use `_ExecuteCapabilityNotSentToken` and
constructs `NoCapabilityRequestBeforeReadiness`; no caller can instantiate or
serialize that token. Any capability-sent path without authenticated response
evidence is `invalid_consumed_attempt`, never a null-transport seal.

After readiness, the target validates both returned objects/hashes, the nested
host status, and their references and freezes only the pre-persistence
`AuthenticatedCredentialResponseEvidence`. It then exclusively create-new
persists the exact returned `P` bytes as
`credential-pipe-lifecycle.json`, reopens and byte-compares them, create-new
persists the exact returned `C` bytes as `credential-lifecycle.json`, and reopens
and byte-compares them beneath the same held prepared-root identity. Only after
both file/parent fsyncs, both byte-identical reopens, and the final root identity/
membership recapture does it construct `PersistedCredentialLifecycleEvidence`
with `persisted_reopen_verified:true`; only then may it freeze
`AuthenticatedCredentialTransport(response_evidence, persisted_lifecycle)`.
No authenticated transport exists before this sequence finishes. The target
never reconstructs an object or hash from counters. Only then may it submit
descriptor-bound case/client requests on the same broker IPC. The target never
receives the pipe handle, credential bytes, spawn environment, or client process
handle.

Lifecycle persistence is two no-follow, create-new, file-and-parent-fsynced
writes to those exact prepared slots in the order above, each followed by a
byte-identical reopen and prepared-root identity/membership recapture. A pre-existing slot, wrong parent,
reparse/hard link, membership drift, partial/unexpected bytes, or absent file
after a post-readiness publication error is `invalid_consumed_attempt`: retain
the state untouched, create no seal/client, and never retry. If an exception is
raised after both exact complete lifecycle records were durably published and
they still reopen under the original identities, do not continue to a client; seal
the one `CAMPAIGN_SECRET_ISOLATION_FAILED` zero-run using that lifecycle. A
completed pre-readiness broker failure leaves both slots proven absent and may
use only the authenticated pre-readiness-response variant; a target-side
failure before the capability send may use only the private not-sent-token
variant.

The root-broker performs no Task 10-through-16 campaign-domain mutation and
cannot import their writers or sealers. It may write only its descriptor-bound
transport/process records and client stdout/stderr captures. Every broker-side
failure is returned to the execute target as one closed secret-free public code
plus the required null-or-two-objects-and-hashes lifecycle projection;
before a first client start the target alone maps that code through the existing
claim-integrity checks to `seal_zero_run_failure`, or leaves the state as
`invalid_consumed_attempt` when those checks do not permit a write. During the
campaign, each client request returns only descriptor-bound public process/
capture evidence. The execute target owns run declarations, ledgers, and
terminal sealing. The root emits its host-facing terminal only after the target
has closed broker requests, observed response EOF, and emitted its own terminal;
no failure text or credential crosses either terminal frame.

Credential lookup, transfer-attempt, transfer-completion, and root-accept counts
remain zero through root
construction, pre-ACK validation, ACK/GO, post-GO revalidation, marker, claim,
client-identity reopen, target capability validation, secret-pipe creation,
connection, and peer validation. After receiving `claim-ready`, the host
independently reopens and revalidates authorization, reservation, marker,
claim, raw-root identity/membership, descriptor nonce, root and target
descriptor/PID/creation-time bindings, client-spec digest, and named-pipe
name record. A missing, malformed, duplicate, replayed, wrong-nonce,
wrong-root/target-PID/time, wrong-marker/claim/spec, or wrong-pipe frame
rejects with all four counts still zero. One valid readiness frame permits only
the single pipe open and peer exchange; it does not permit credential lookup.
Only one subsequent canonical `credential-peer-accepted` frame followed by the
fresh repeated host revalidation permits at most one lookup of the single named
host credential and one host-to-execute-root transfer attempt. Replay or a
second lookup/attempt is forbidden.

The credential transport version is exactly
`complete-suite-provider-credential-pipe-v1`; loopback specs instead use
`complete-suite-no-credential-v1` and cannot carry a pipe or credential. For an
execute run, define `P` and the name exactly as:

```text
P = first 32 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256(
    ASCII(
        "complete-suite-provider-credential-pipe-v1\n"
        + root_descriptor_nonce + "\n"
        + target_descriptor_nonce + "\n"
        + provider_attempt_claim_sha256 + "\n"
    )
)
credential_pipe_name = "\\\\.\\pipe\\kokoroarc-c6-execute-" + P
credential_pipe_name_sha256 = SHA-256(ASCII(credential_pipe_name))
host_status_pipe_name = "\\\\.\\pipe\\kokoroarc-c6-execute-status-" + P
host_status_pipe_name_sha256 = SHA-256(ASCII(host_status_pipe_name))
```

The name grammar bytes are exactly
`complete-suite-execute-credential-pipe-name-v1\n\\.\pipe\kokoroarc-c6-execute-<32-lowercase-hex>\n`;
their fixed SHA-256 is
`29078e6b8f6b81c33cbd530d75d50af49d57efeb7cbf178772b6991ceb90dba7`.
Validation is ordinal and requires the exact prefix, exactly 32 lowercase hex
characters, exact total length, and no suffix, alternate case, slash form, UNC
host, or caller-supplied name. `ExecuteCredentialPipeName` repeats both nonces,
the claim hash, transport version, payload cap, value hash, and grammar digest
and is embedded in `ExecuteClaimReady`. The paired host-status name grammar is
exactly
`complete-suite-execute-credential-host-status-pipe-name-v1\n\\.\pipe\kokoroarc-c6-execute-status-<32-lowercase-hex>\n`;
its fixed SHA-256 is
`9c3c0b32ef2fc6d043800293ae1cb964fc0a212a9107472e9a8326c855be7837`.
`ExecuteCredentialHostStatusPipeName` binds the same nonces, claim, transport,
65,536-byte payload cap, exact value/hash, and this grammar digest. Readiness
nests both name records. Neither name is caller supplied, and neither record
depends on a later status or lifecycle hash.

`ExecuteCredentialPeerAccepted` is canonical compact strict-ASCII JSON plus
one LF. Its serialized keys are exactly the dataclass fields in order through
`root_creation_time`; `canonical_sha256` is a wrapper field and is not
serialized. It binds the accepted capability, claim, both pipe-name hashes, and both
peer PID/creation-time identities and contains no credential, credential
length/hash, path, or private error text.

The root creates the first and only credential-data server instance with exact
arguments:

```text
dwOpenMode = PIPE_ACCESS_INBOUND | FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE |
             FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED
dwPipeMode = PIPE_TYPE_BYTE | PIPE_READMODE_BYTE | PIPE_WAIT |
             PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS
nMaxInstances = 1
nOutBufferSize = 0
nInBufferSize = 65540
nDefaultTimeOut = 0
SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES.bInheritHandle = FALSE
```

It creates the first and only host-status server with the same arguments and
`nInBufferSize = 65540`; that channel carries exactly one length-prefixed
canonical status JSON frame and EOF, never credential data. Both owners are the
root's current `TokenUser` SID. Each DACL is present,
non-defaulted, protected, and contains exactly one explicit zero-flag allow ACE
for that SID with `FILE_GENERIC_WRITE`; there is no inherited, group, world,
anonymous, system, or additional ACE. No credential or host-status pipe handle is inheritable
or appears in a descriptor or `HANDLE_LIST`. The root requeries the owner/DACL
of both servers before readiness and the host requeries both after opening and
before lookup.

The root associates both servers with its completion port under distinct typed
credential-data and credential-host-status keys, issues exactly one overlapped
`ConnectNamedPipe` on each, accepts only `FALSE/ERROR_IO_PENDING` for each, and
then emits `claim-ready`. A synchronous success, `ERROR_PIPE_CONNECTED`, or any
other initial result on either server proves an unauthorized pre-readiness race
and fails closed. After validating `claim-ready`, the host calls `CreateFileW`
exactly once for each bound name with `GENERIC_WRITE`, share mode zero,
`OPEN_EXISTING`, and `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED | SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT |
SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION`; there is no `WaitNamedPipe`, retry, reconnect, second
open, `DisconnectNamedPipe`, or instance reuse on either channel. Before any
write, the host associates both client handles with its private completion port
under distinct typed credential-data-write and credential-host-status-write
keys. For each handle, the host queries the server with only
`PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION` and requires its PID/creation time to equal
the authenticated root. The root consumes both connect completions, applies the
analogous minimum-rights query to both clients, requires the same descriptor-
bound host PID/creation time on both, and only then emits one canonical
`ExecuteCredentialPeerAccepted` frame binding both pipe-name hashes on
ACK/status. The host must validate that frame and freshly repeat the
authorization/state checks above before its sole credential lookup. A
connection, association, identity, status-frame, or fresh-state mismatch
permanently consumes both one-shot instances with all four counters zero.

The sole frame is unsigned 32-bit little-endian `N`, exactly `N` payload bytes,
writer close, and exact EOF. `N == 0` is the only
`credential-unavailable` control frame: it carries no credential, creates no
`ProviderCredential`, maps to `CAMPAIGN_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, and requires
immediate EOF. `1 <= N <= 65536` is a credential candidate; `N > 65536`
rejects before payload allocation. The root reads the four-byte prefix and any
payload incrementally, then issues one bounded extra one-byte read and accepts
only EOF/`ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE`. Early EOF, a partial prefix/payload, trailing
byte, second frame/connection, or missing EOF maps to
`CAMPAIGN_SECRET_ISOLATION_FAILED`.

Only after the authenticated `credential-peer-accepted` frame and fresh host
revalidation does the host atomically increment
`credential_lookup_count`, obtains only `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and validates the
original UTF-16 value character-by-character before encoding with a strict
failure fallback. NUL, space, control, non-ASCII, surrogate, empty, or over-cap
values are never trimmed, normalized, hashed, logged, or length-retained; the
host writes the four zero bytes and closes. For a valid nonzero candidate, it
first writes and dequeues the four-byte prefix, then increments
`credential_transfer_attempt_count` immediately before the first payload write,
forbids retry, and increments
`credential_transfer_completion_count` only after every prefix/payload write
completion is dequeued and the writer closes. The root increments
`credential_frame_accept_count` only after a nonzero payload passes visible-
ASCII `0x21..0x7e`, exact-length, and immediate-EOF validation.

The four counters never exceed one and have exactly these terminal values:

| outcome | lookup | transfer attempt | host completion | root credential accept |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| any pre-lookup failure | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| prefix is incomplete/undecodable, or unavailable framing is rejected | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| complete `N=0` unavailable frame | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| nonzero frame starts but host write fails | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| host completes nonzero frame; root rejects framing/EOF | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| accepted nonzero credential | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

The host-status payload is exactly one compact strict-ASCII JSON object plus one
LF, framed by one unsigned four-byte little-endian payload length and followed
by writer close/EOF. Its canonical keys are exactly
`CredentialHostStatus` in dataclass order through
`host_mutable_buffers_scrubbed_or_absent`; `canonical_sha256` is a wrapper field
and is not serialized. Its host-only tuple is closed:

| host outcome | frame/progress | lookup | attempt | completion |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `pre-lookup-failure` | `none/none/not-applicable` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `credential-unavailable` | `unavailable/complete/not-applicable` | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `host-transfer-failure` | intended frame kind plus the actual coarse incomplete prefix/payload class | 1 | 0 or 1 | 0 |
| `host-transfer-complete` | `nonzero/complete/complete` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

For `host-transfer-failure`, attempt is one if and only if the first nonzero
payload write was issued; prefix and payload progress must agree with the exact
retired write cursor, but no byte count is retained. Any other tuple, unknown or
second status frame, over-cap frame, trailing byte, missing EOF, binding/hash or
peer-identity mismatch is invalid. The status contains neither `N`, credential
bytes, an exact/rounded payload length, a transferred-byte count, nor any
credential- or length-derived hash.

Only `(1,1,1,1)` permits client environment materialization. On every terminal
path each side freezes new work, calls `CancelIoEx` for each outstanding
connect/read/write, and consumes every completion. After no host I/O can still
reference its credential-data buffers, the host closes the credential-data
writer exactly once, best-effort overwrites every allocated mutable payload/
frame, and constructs the status only from immutable bindings and the coarse
table above. It then writes and retires that single status frame, closes the
status writer, and waits for no root response before doing so. The status field
`credential_data_writer_outstanding_io_final` covers only the already closed
data writer; the root proves status-channel retirement independently by
observing its frame, EOF, and zero outstanding status reads. The root pumps both
channels concurrently and never waits for status before draining credential
data. It overwrites mutable prefix/payload buffers after its data reads retire,
then closes both servers exactly once. Kernel pipe buffers and immutable strings
are explicitly not claimed zeroized. No transport error, exception, counter
record, process record, terminal frame, or broker response contains credential
bytes.

For every completed broker response, the root constructs exactly one canonical
`CredentialHostStatus`, one canonical root-side
`CredentialPipeLifecycleRecord`, and one canonical `CredentialLifecycleRecord`
if and only if it successfully emitted canonical `ExecuteClaimReady` and then
received and authenticated the one host-status frame and its EOF. A controlled
failure after a capability request but before readiness returns one authenticated
canonical broker-failure response with neither lifecycle object; all four
counters remain zero and every lifecycle response/terminal field below is JSON
`null`. A capability-sent path without those exact authenticated response bytes
and hash is consumed-invalid, not a controlled null projection. Once
readiness was emitted, cleanup and completion draining are mandatory. An
orderly response must carry both lifecycle objects even when fresh host
revalidation, lookup, transfer, framing, or credential-data EOF fails; absent,
malformed, unauthenticated, incoherent, or unterminated host status cannot be
turned into such a response and is `invalid_consumed_attempt`.

The root verifies the host status against readiness, both peer identities, its
own data-pipe observations, and the host counter/progress table. It then nests
the exact status object and its hash in `CredentialPipeLifecycleRecord`; only
after both pipe lifecycles are terminal does it construct
`CredentialLifecycleRecord`, whose host counters and cleanup literal must equal
the nested status and whose `credential_host_status_sha256` must equal that
same hash. Thus the acyclic authority order is host status `H`, pipe lifecycle
`P(H)`, credential lifecycle `C(H_sha256,P_sha256)`, then broker response.

The
`CredentialLifecycleRecord` compact strict-ASCII JSON plus one LF serializes
exactly the dataclass fields in order through
`credential_pipe_lifecycle_sha256`; `canonical_sha256` is a wrapper field and
is not serialized. The `CredentialPipeLifecycleRecord` is independently compact
strict-ASCII JSON plus one LF with serialized fields in dataclass order through
`host_status_server_closed`; its wrapper hash is excluded. Its two byte caps are
the fixed literals 65,540; it deliberately has no actual credential-data byte
count, payload byte count, payload length/hash, or credential value: prefix and payload
state are only the closed progress classes shown in the schema. The credential-
pipe lifecycle hash is the hash of that returned root-side record, which must
later appear byte-identically in the same execute-root process record. The host's distinct credential-write completion key and
lifecycle remain in host-control-plane accounting and must reconcile to the
same byte/completion/close outcome before that process record is accepted.
Credential-data endpoints on both sides are excluded from generic
`PipeLifecycleRecord`: its `bytes_transferred` field is never populated or
hashed for this transport. Host-side exact write lengths exist only transiently
while the already secret-bearing host performs I/O; they are compared to the
secret-free `CredentialHostStatus` progress/counter projection, never serialized
or hashed, and are discarded with the mutable frame. The status channel itself
is represented by the fixed cap, frame/EOF/error/cancellation/close facts in
`CredentialPipeLifecycleRecord`; its exact transferred count may be retained
because its payload is secret-free. Durable host terminal data repeats only the
secret-free lifecycle hashes, progress classes, counters, and cleanup result.
Both lifecycle objects have the same `frame_kind`. It is `none` before lookup,
`indeterminate` after lookup until the full four-byte prefix is decoded,
`unavailable` only for decoded `N=0`, and `nonzero` for any decoded positive N,
including an over-cap value that is rejected before allocation. Prefix progress
records only none/partial/complete. Payload progress is `not-applicable` unless
frame kind is nonzero and otherwise records only none/partial/complete. These
classes plus EOF/error/cancellation/close facts are sufficient for the outcome
mapping below and never retain or make a digest oracle for the payload length.
An abrupt root termination after readiness that prevents this response is not
converted into a null lifecycle or a sealed transport outcome: the host records
the missing-response protocol failure, the consumed attempt is
`invalid_consumed_attempt`, no campaign seal or client is permitted, and no
retry is available.

The lifecycle outcome and booleans are closed projections of `frame_kind`, the
counter tuple, and the referenced credential-pipe completion facts.
`pre-lookup-failure` is `frame_kind="none"` and exactly `(0,0,0,0)`.
`credential-unavailable` is `frame_kind="unavailable"`, exactly `(1,0,0,0)`,
and an exact completed four-byte `N=0` plus EOF. `host-transfer-failure` is an
incomplete host write with indeterminate/`(1,0,0,0)`,
unavailable/`(1,0,0,0)`, or nonzero/`(1,1,0,0)`.
`root-frame-rejection` is a host-complete unavailable/`(1,0,0,0)` or
nonzero/`(1,1,1,0)` frame whose root framing/EOF validation failed.
`credential-accepted` is nonzero/`(1,1,1,1)`. No other combination is valid.
`provider_credential_created` is true if and only if the outcome is
`credential-accepted`. `peer_accepted_sha256` is null until a canonical
peer-accepted frame was successfully emitted and is its exact hash thereafter;
therefore a post-peer fresh-state rejection is still `pre-lookup-failure` with
a non-null peer hash. Each `*_mutable_buffers_scrubbed_or_absent` literal means
that every mutable buffer actually allocated by that side was overwrite-
attempted in `finally`, not that kernel buffers or immutable strings were
zeroized.

Only an execute root that returned the post-readiness lifecycles embeds that
same credential object in `GuardedProcessRecord.credential_lifecycle` and that
same pipe object in `pipe_lifecycles`; every other guarded
process and any execute root without such a completed response serializes that
field as null. A null execute-root lifecycle after observed readiness is a fatal
missing-response mismatch, never an ordinary pre-readiness result. The execute
root's final host-facing terminal
repeats both null-or-hash projections, and the host accepts it only after matching
the exact `CredentialHostStatus` it sent, its own write-completion accounting,
mutable-buffer cleanup, and the root-side `CredentialPipeLifecycleRecord`. The execute target reopens the
two persisted lifecycle records and repeats the same projections in its terminal.
`provider-attempt-terminal.json`, whose branches
all precede raw-root claim and readiness, has the two closed fields
`credential_pipe_lifecycle_sha256:null` and
`credential_lifecycle_sha256:null`. Every claimed-root campaign ledger,
completion, inventory, and seal has both closed nullable hash fields; all four records must agree with the target and
root process terminals. A normal 24-run completion or any started-run terminal
requires both non-null hashes and a `credential-accepted` lifecycle. A sealed
zero-run before readiness requires both null; one after readiness requires the
exact non-null pipe/lifecycle pair for its terminal transport outcome. The
sealed-campaign auditor reopens both lifecycle files, recomputes their canonical
hashes and reference, and requires
this entire cross-record projection before classifying any consumed attempt. No
hash may be synthesized from counters alone or supplied independently by the
execute target.

The execute root itself—not a guarded target or a second broker—receives that
one-use frame and retains the one scoped credential only until the 24-run
campaign reaches terminal broker shutdown. For each later authenticated client
request it independently reopens the launch evidence, materializes one fresh
spawn-only environment, and uses the reviewed constructor to create only that
descriptor-bound `codex-client-root`, with at most 24 total and four concurrent.
The secret is never canonicalized, hashed, persisted, logged, echoed, placed on
argv, returned over broker IPC, or put in an agent-shell environment. The
explicit unavoidable-copy account is: host environment string, host mutable
transfer frame, OS pipe buffers, root receive bytes/scoped string, each
per-client root mapping, each root-created UTF-16 client environment block, the
OS-created Codex process environment, and any immutable copies retained by the
client TCB. The latter two persist for the client lifetime and are not broker-
zeroizable. Host drops its immutable reference after transfer; the root drops
its scoped immutable reference only after final/terminal shutdown. Both sides
best-effort overwrite only mutable host frames, root receive buffers, per-client
mappings, and root-created UTF-16 blocks as soon as their corresponding use
ends; the plan makes no zero-copy or immutable-string-zeroization claim. A no-credential loopback
`materialize_spawn_environment` call is permitted only in the corresponding
client-preflight root-broker; a credential-bearing call is permitted only in
this execute root-broker after authenticated peer acceptance and credential
frame acceptance. It is never callable
in a guarded target or native leaf, and no non-`execute` role can create a
secret channel.

After the Task 9 trust anchor, `Invoke-C6Git` is the only Git process
constructor in the committed control plane, broker, tests, and runbooks. The
committed instance accepts only a closed role
literal plus that role's recursively exact ordered binding schema; unknown,
missing, reordered, or wrong-typed fields reject before construction. Neither
entrypoint accepts argv, revision expressions, path roles, environment, timeout,
or output-policy passthrough. The closed roles cover identity reads, local-
object proof/cat-file, exact diff/status, each literal task stage/commit,
provisional `write-tree`, and A/B materialization. The launcher pins/locks the
one Git PE, constructs the environment from empty with fixed OS and fresh
HOME/XDG/temp values, rejects every inherited `GIT_*`, disables system/global config, and
forces hooks, signing, filters/external diff/merge, fsmonitor, credentials and
prompts, editors/pagers, maintenance, lazy fetch, transports, remote helpers,
submodules, and protocol rewrites off. Before object use it parses every config
origin/scope and repository control file no-follow. The sole effective-config
read is exactly `git config --null --list --show-origin --show-scope --name-only
--no-includes`; its raw capture is retained only in trusted process memory and
is never emitted. Before that child, the broker uses the process-free linked-
worktree resolver above to bind `.git`, its admin directory/`commondir`, the
common config, and absent worktree config. The fixed output parser then accepts
sensitive override names only as exact command-scope tuples from the literal
prefix and publishes only enum counts plus the tuple-set digest; the same check
runs before every other Git command. It rejects aliases, hooks, filters,
credentials, signing, promisor/partial-clone,
submodule, unsafe protocol/URL rewrite, alternates, shallow/graft/replace, or
unexpected A/B settings. Existing remote metadata may be recorded as inert
only when every transport is disabled and no role grammar can name it. With
`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, it proves every referenced commit/tree/blob exists in the
single local object database before use. Each Git child uses the same bounded
64 KiB-chunk native core, role deadline, exact standalone `L0` or brokered
`[J1,T0,...,Tk,Ln]` Job-topology row, zero descendants,
strict text or binary `-z` parser, and locked identity postcheck. Only the exact
A/B materialization roles may differ by their frozen `core.autocrlf` value.

Task 9 REDs mechanically scan all approval-bound Python/PowerShell and this
plan's executable fences after the trust transition. They reject raw `git`, a second Git
`ProcessStartInfo`, `Start-Process`, every Python launch other than the one exact
fixed-loader vector above (including bare `python -B`, `python -m`, `& $python`,
a Python-valued `Invoke-C6Native`, or arbitrary `-c`), `ReadToEnd*`, `StreamReader`
replacement decoding, and any post-EOF-only cap. They also exercise suspended
creation, exact handles, ACK/GO replay, secret-before-GO, wrong pipe peer,
missing evaluation envelope, output cap, deadline, partial read, malformed
UTF-8, child attempt, config/include/hook/filter/remote/lazy-fetch mutants, and
advisory-Job-message loss plus final accounting mismatch. Pre-trust
C6-HOST-TEST/C6-HOST-COMMIT and explanatory
`text` fences are parsed separately; they may show logical requests, but can
never be executed as PowerShell or counted as a post-transition operator
exception.

The operator surface after the trust anchor is therefore only:

```text
Invoke-C6Git -Role <closed-role> -Bindings <closed ordered values>
Invoke-C6RootPython -Role <closed-role> -Bindings <closed ordered values>
new fixed console-host/outer-PowerShell/inner-Python helper chain: <one fixed human-authorization artifact request>
new fixed console-host/outer-PowerShell/inner-Python helper chain: <one fixed host-review envelope or result request>
platform collaboration: <the one exact pre-trust c6_task9_artifact_oracle_review envelope and bounded result>
spawn_agent <one already-published HostReviewEvaluationEnvelope>
```

The last four are distinct host operations, not hidden root/native/client
constructors. The platform-collaboration row is the single pre-trust oracle
review call and grants the reviewer no child-agent authority. `spawn_agent` is
permitted only for the six later closed host-review roles, after the exact
envelope exists; it returns only the bounded final result and may not spawn a
child. Thus these rows account for exactly seven host collaboration calls while
leaving the later six-role registry unchanged. Every other action remains
behind the two committed control-plane entrypoints.

Every behavior or policy change follows RED, minimal GREEN, focused regression,
then commit. If an expected RED test passes, inspect the test before writing
implementation. If an unrelated test fails, use
`superpowers:systematic-debugging` rather than broadening the change.

```python
def command_provenance_version(
    campaign_bytes: bytes,
    *,
    expected_campaign_sha256: str,
) -> str:
    campaign = _decode_canonical_campaign_bytes(
        campaign_bytes,
        expected_sha256=expected_campaign_sha256,
    )
    provenance = campaign.get("command_provenance")
    if provenance is None:
        return LEGACY_COMMAND_PROVENANCE_VERSION
    if not isinstance(provenance, dict):
        raise RuntimeError("command_provenance_version")
    version = provenance.get("version")
    if version != COMMAND_PLAN_PROVENANCE_VERSION:
        raise RuntimeError("command_provenance_version")
    return version
```

Do not alter `_structured_command`, `_command_records`, or any historical result
logic in this task. `_decode_canonical_campaign_bytes` duplicate-key-decodes a
fresh private view, verifies exact canonical bytes/hash, and never exposes or
retains a caller-owned mapping.

Test an absolute frozen shell path followed by exactly:

```text
-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command <one quoted payload field>
```

Cover both frozen renderer encodings:

- single-quoted field with doubled single quotes;
- double-quoted field with the renderer's exact backslash/quote escaping.

The rendered record is strict UTF-8 with no BOM or terminal newline. It starts
with the double-quoted absolute shell path, then exactly one ASCII space between
each flag/value. For `quote_style="single"`, the payload field is one leading
and trailing ASCII apostrophe and every payload apostrophe is doubled; all other
payload bytes are unchanged. For `quote_style="double"`, the field uses the
Windows argv display rule: a run of `n` backslashes immediately before a
literal quote becomes `2n+1` backslashes plus the quote, a trailing run of `n`
backslashes becomes `2n` before the closing quote, and all other bytes are
unchanged. No alternate but equivalent spacing or quoting is accepted.

Require strict UTF-8 decode, extract/decode/re-render byte equality, and
separate byte lengths plus hashes for the full event, payload field, and
decoded UTF-8 payload.

```text
decode_file_change_lifecycles(

    *,

authorize_command_plan(

authorize_file_change_events(

    retained_session_bytes: bytes,
    content_sources: tuple[FileChangeContentSource, ...],
    *,
    context: FileChangePolicyContext,

```

`BoundFilesystemEvidence` is built only from canonical, duplicate-key-rejected
`pre-run-state.json` and `post-run-state.json` bytes. The runner captures every
approved read/output root and its existing ancestor chain with one bounded
no-follow direct-scandir traversal before the first client callback and again
after the client exits. Unlike the legacy file-only inventory, the v1 snapshot
includes plain directories and root presence, so an absent directory and an
existing empty directory have different canonical bytes. Each entry binds
type, identity, reparse tag, link count, and—for files—size/content SHA-256.
Roots and entries are sorted, unique, capped at 4,096 entries per root and the
existing 64 MiB aggregate, and rechecked for membership/identity stability.
Created, changed, and removed sets are derived from the two snapshots and
verified against the retained post-run fields. The immutable context contains
only tuples/scalars; no caller-owned mapping or list survives construction.

`CommandPolicyDecision` preserves the decoder's statement/pipeline grouping;
operation indices are global within that one command record and carry their
exact statement and optional pipeline index. Its closed `record_class` is
derived—not caller supplied—from topology: `read_only_pipeline` is exactly one
statement containing one approved read pipeline (one scalar read or one closed
multi-stage read projection), `help_discovery` is exactly one help statement,
and every record with operational JSON is `operational_json`. Two semicolon-
separated reads, two pipelines, a read plus help, or a forged class/topology hash
rejects. The canonical decision bytes/hash bind grouping and class for Task 6.

`FileChangeContentSource` carries paths only; callers cannot submit already-
materialized or claimed content bytes. `authorize_file_change_events` is the sole
content factory. Before allocating a payload buffer it revalidates the approval-
bound sanitizer ledger identity/hash, loads each named sanitizer record with a
64 KiB cap and duplicate-key rejection, and proves the record belongs to that
ledger. It lstat/open-fstat/post-fstat/post-lstat-checks each raw/retained path
against the corresponding post snapshot and sanitizer transform, checks the
declared/per-file/aggregate sizes before and during 64 KiB chunked reads, and
rejects EOF/extra-byte/identity/hash drift. `BoundFileChangeContent` and
`FileChangePolicyDecision` have no public initializer; one module-private
factory creates them only after every check succeeds, and every consumer rejects
an uninitialized or subclassed value. A forged record digest, direct bound-
object construction, oversized stat, lying size, or callback mutation therefore
fails before semantic parsing. The internal raw-bearing object is private,
`repr=False`, and never leaves the function; raw buffers are discarded after
validation. The decision retains only raw size/hash, immutable retained bytes/
size/hash, canonical document hashes, validation hash, and sanitizer-record hash,
and its repr/errors contain only bounded counts/digests.

Freeze a file-change resource account independent of session JSONL and command
output: at most 64 logical started/completed lifecycles and 256 ordered path/kind
entries per run; at most 128 unique final documents; at most 262,144 bytes in
either the raw or retained form of one document; at most 32 MiB raw, 32 MiB
retained, and 64 MiB combined. Count every repeated `add`/`update` entry toward
256 and each final path once toward 128. Before schema dispatch, reject semantic
depth above 64, more than 8,192 nodes, more than 1,024 members in one collection,
or a scalar above 16,384 Unicode code points; reject YAML aliases and merge
keys. Then apply stricter production bounds: source-pack 128 files, 256,000
bytes/file, 2,000,000 bytes total, depth six; corpus 64,000 bytes/file, 192,000
total, depth 16, 4,096 scalar characters, 256 members, 4,096 nodes, and 128
cases/file. Crossing any bound stops before unbounded allocation or document
decoding. The 64 MiB/50,000-line session JSONL and 4 MiB/128-document command
output accounts remain separate.

Freeze one symmetric maximum-optional case policy for both variants. An unused
allowed path is not a missing transition. `original-authoring-route` may change
only these exact paths below `data\authoring\mika-moongear`: `request.json`,
`character.yaml`; the seven component files `identity.yaml`, `evidence.yaml`,
`derived-profile.yaml`, `overrides.yaml`, `behavior.yaml`, `growth.yaml`, and
`expressions.yaml`; `locales\en-US.yaml`, `locales\ja-JP.yaml`, and
`locales\zh-CN.yaml`; `scenarios\debugging.yaml`; `tests\positive.yaml`,
`tests\negative.yaml`, `tests\multilingual.yaml`, and
`tests\protected-spans.yaml`; and `validation\request-validate-1.json`,
`request-validate-2.json`, `draft-validate-1.json`, and
`draft-validate-2.json`. `workspace-override-explicit-activation` may change only
the five exact scratch paths
`data\policy-workspace-demo-input.json`,
`data\semantic-workspace-demo.json`,
`data\policy-workspace-demo.json`, `data\plan-workspace-demo.json`, and
`data\rendered-workspace-demo.json`. Both baseline and suite-enabled receive
the same allowed surface; an observed trace may use none, some, or all of it.
The other ten cases have an empty file-change rules tuple in both variants.
This freezes authorization, not an Approved5 action trace.

Each rule freezes its schema/loader role, exact producing or consuming action
prefixes, and—where it mirrors CLI output—the selected JSON member. The four
validation files select the whole corresponding result document; the compiled
policy selects `policy`; the render plan selects `plan`. The policy input,
semantic result, and rendered output are consumer inputs. No role may be
reassigned dynamically from event content.

Full parameter names are matched case-insensitively and emitted in canonical
casing; aliases and abbreviations are never accepted. Positive cases are
limited to:

- direct literal `kokoro`;
- literal call operator targeting exact `.tools\kokoro.cmd`;
- `Get-Content`, `Get-ChildItem`, `Test-Path`, `Get-FileHash`,
  `Select-Object`, `Sort-Object`, and `rg` with the exact v1 table below;
- pipelines whose every stage is independently allowlisted and has no script
  block; and
- literal missing-directory creation under a declared output root when that
  directory is an ancestor of a CLI output declared in the same record, through
  the exact `New-Item ... | Out-Null` shape defined below.

The closed read parameter table is:

| Command | Exact v1 operands and parameters |
| --- | --- |
| `Get-Content` | Exactly one literal filesystem path, either positional or `-LiteralPath`; optional `-Raw`; optional exact `-ErrorAction Stop`. |
| `Get-ChildItem` | Exactly one literal filesystem path, either positional or `-LiteralPath`; optional one of `-File` or `-Directory`; optional `-Name`; optional one of `-Recurse` or `-Depth 0..8`; optional exact `-ErrorAction Stop`. A recursive root must pass a no-follow pre-scan capped at 4,096 entries. |
| `Test-Path` | Exactly one literal filesystem path, either positional or `-LiteralPath`; optional `-PathType Leaf` or `-PathType Container`; optional exact `-ErrorAction Stop`. |
| `Get-FileHash` | Exactly one literal regular-file path, either positional or `-LiteralPath`; optional `-Algorithm SHA256` only; optional exact `-ErrorAction Stop`. |
| `Select-Object` | Pipeline-only; exactly one of `-First 1..256`, `-Last 1..256`, or `-Property` with exactly one name from `Name,Length,Hash,Path,FullName,LastWriteTimeUtc`. Arrays, `-ExpandProperty`, `-Skip`, and calculated properties reject. |
| `Sort-Object` | Pipeline-only; optional `-Property` with one name from `Name,Length,Hash,Path,FullName,LastWriteTimeUtc`; optional `-Unique`. |
| `rg` | Exact frozen executable identity and exact order. Form A: `rg --files --color never` then 0..16 `--glob <literal>` pairs then one literal approved root. Form B: `rg --fixed-strings --color never`, optional `--line-number`, optional `--no-heading`, required `--max-count <1..256>`, then one literal pattern, 0..16 `--glob <literal>` pairs, and one literal approved path/root. No duplicate flag. Every root first passes the same bounded no-follow pre-scan capped at 4,096 entries. |

The policy does not import or introspect `argparse` at adjudication time. It
contains the following frozen `complete-suite-kokoro-cli-v1` table. Every row
requires one final `--json`, consumes options in the displayed order, rejects
duplicates and omitted required values, and rejects every token not described
by the row. A path value is one parser-proved literal, normalized and confined
to the row's approved read/output class. An identifier matches
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}`; locale is exactly `en-US`, `ja-JP`, or
`zh-CN`; scope is exactly `global` or `workspace`, with `--workspace` required
iff scope is `workspace`. Bracketed clauses are optional; alternatives joined
by `|` are mutually exclusive.

Every decoded argv literal is at most 4,096 UTF-8 bytes, including path,
pattern, glob, identifier, and option-value literals; the complete decoded
PowerShell payload remains capped at 256 KiB. Apply the literal cap before path
resolution, pattern compilation, allocation, or filesystem access. Add exact-at
and one-byte-over tests for a path, `rg` pattern, glob, and non-ASCII literal.

| Literal action prefix | Exact remaining v1 operands/options before `--json` | Declared output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pack validate` / `pack compile` | one existing pack path | none |
| `pack install` | one existing `.karc` path; `--scope <scope>`; [`--workspace <case-workspace>`]; [`--dry-run`] | none |
| `pack list` | `--scope <scope>`; [`--workspace <case-workspace>`] | none |
| `pack export` | `--compiled <read-path>`; `--promotion <read-path>`; `--hard-report <read-path>`; `--soft-report <read-path>`; [`--publication-report <read-path>`]; `--out <output-path>` | `--out` |

The table intentionally excludes `config default clear`, `session end`,
`pack remove`, `state reset`, `consent grant/revoke`, `suite install`, archive
migration/compatibility, and every network/publication command because no
Campaign 6 case authorizes those mutations. Help-only discovery is a separate
nonoperational grammar: `kokoro`, any proper action-prefix of a row above, or a
complete row prefix followed by the sole flag `--help`. It has no declared
output, may not share a record with operational JSON, and is never passed to an
action-specific evidence check.

The `session start` positive matrix must include the immutable
`explicit-character-precedence` route with both `--character` and `--workspace`
present: the explicit character is the selected input while the workspace and
global defaults remain unchanged. Exercise both allowed option orders. Reject a
duplicate option, an order outside the two displayed forms, a workspace outside
the case root, or an explicit character outside the approved identifier/read-
path class. The policy authorizes only the literal operation; the later
case-specific adjudicator proves the precedence result from retained evidence.

Every path operand is a single parser-proved literal under an approved read
root. Array literals, wildcard expansion, provider-qualified paths, `-Path`,
`-Filter`, `-Include`, `-Exclude`, `-Hidden`, `--hidden`, `--follow`,
`--pre`, config loading, and all parameters not shown in the table reject.
`RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` is set to the platform null device.

Silent directory creation accepts exactly literal `New-Item` with
`-ItemType Directory`, exactly one literal `-Path` or `-LiteralPath`, optional
exact `-ErrorAction Stop`, no `-Force`, and a pipeline only to parameterless
`Out-Null`. The target must be absent from the bound pre-run directory-aware
snapshot, present as one newly created plain directory in the bound post-run
snapshot/created set, no-follow below one declared output root, and an ancestor
of at least one newly created `declared_output_paths` file extracted from a
recognized CLI operation in the same top-level record. Existing ancestor/root
identities must agree across the snapshots. Positive regressions cover both
`outputs` (the Approved5 calibration shape) and `data\compiled`; neither
directory name is hardcoded in policy. The identical plan and post tree with a
pre-existing empty target must reject, as must a reparse target, ancestor/root
identity drift, a missing/extra created-path entry, or a declared output that
does not make the matching absent-to-created transition.

Operational CLI evidence requires unconditional top-level execution, `--json`,
no pipeline, no redirection, no backgrounding, and no help flag.

Direct literal `kokoro` is authorized only when deterministic Windows resolution
against `shell_path_entries` and `shell_pathext` yields the exact case-local
`.tools\kokoro.cmd` as the first and unique match. Literal call-operator use must
name that same path. Both require its frozen digest and
`shell_environment_sha256`; a later PATH, PATHEXT, shim, or environment change
rejects.

Freeze exactly one expected-refusal policy row. In case
`archive-overwrite-pressure`, a sole `pack export` operation whose `--out` is
the declared pre-existing `outputs\existing.karc` is tagged
`expected_outcome="expected_refusal"` with expected error code `OUTPUT_EXISTS`.
The later fresh output remains `expected_outcome="success"`. No other case,
action, path, or error code can receive this tag, and a refusal-tagged operation
may not share its command record with another operational CLI invocation.

The installed Codex 0.149.0 contract has one merged completed-event field named
`aggregated_output`; it does not expose separate per-command stdout/stderr
streams. Each `CommandCapturePair` points into corresponding raw and retained
`session.jsonl` completed events. No task invents shell redirection or treats
per-process `stderr.txt` as command output. The existing run-integrity gate
continues to bind and require the Codex-process stderr contract separately.

`bind_session_cli_results` is the sole budget owner. It accepts the complete
source-ordered command tuple for one session, requires consecutive command
indices and strictly increasing nonoverlapping started/completed ordinals,
matches raw/retained event IDs and normalized plans, and folds each domain from
zero exactly once. The v1 limits are hard-coded at 64 MiB for the raw session
and 64 MiB for the retained session. No caller-provided budget, reset, larger
limit, record reuse, skipped record, or out-of-order call exists. The binder
always binds both no-follow session identities, event IDs/ordinals, closed byte
spans, quoted JSON field bytes, decoded merged-output bytes, exact hashes, exits,
decisions, and cumulative counts, including records with no operational JSON.

For N greater than zero, parse exactly N ordered top-level JSON objects for N
operational `--json` operations independently in raw and retained output. Permit
UTF-8 whitespace only between and around documents and use duplicate-key-
rejecting decoders. Require equivalent success/refusal topology and selectors
across domains; retain only the raw canonical document digest plus retained
canonical UTF-8/LF bytes/digest. Every observer receives a fresh detached object
decoded from `retained_document_bytes`; mutating a view cannot affect another
view or the trusted bytes/hash.

For N equal to zero, require the whole record to be exactly one policy-approved
nonoperational class: one read-only pipeline or one help/discovery invocation;
outer exit code zero; valid UTF-8 merged output with no BOM; at most 4 MiB for
the record; no more than the remaining session budget; and empty Codex-process
stderr under the separately bound run-level contract. Bounded non-JSON text or
empty output is allowed. Return zero `BoundCliResult` objects for that command.
Silent-directory support is not an N=0 class: it remains outputless and
must share one N>0 record with the matching declared CLI output. A
nonoperational record can never satisfy an action-specific assertion, and a
record containing an operational JSON command can never use this text branch or
mix inspection/help text into its JSON stream.

Freeze this complete v1 failure enum and condition map:

| Code | Only condition class |
| --- | --- |
| `COMMAND_WRAPPER_INVALID` | outer bytes/UTF-8/quoting/argv shape invalid |
| `COMMAND_WRAPPER_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` | shell path/hash/version mismatch |
| `COMMAND_PAYLOAD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | decoded payload exceeds 256 KiB |
| `COMMAND_EVENT_LIFECYCLE_INVALID` | missing/nonterminal/duplicate started or completed event, or noninteger exit |
| `COMMAND_EVENT_PAIR_MISMATCH` | event ID or exact pre-sanitization command bytes differ |
| `FILE_CHANGE_EVENT_LIFECYCLE_INVALID` | missing/nonterminal/duplicate started or completed file-change item, unsupported state-changing item type, or invalid kind |
| `FILE_CHANGE_RAW_RETAINED_MISMATCH` | event topology or normalized raw/retained path/kind plan differs |
| `FILE_CHANGE_POLICY_DENIED` | variant/case/path/role/kind is outside the closed file-change policy |
| `FILE_CHANGE_PATH_UNSAFE` | add/update transition, root, ancestry, link, identity, membership, or snapshot binding fails |
| `FILE_CHANGE_CONTENT_INVALID` | content size/hash/sanitizer/UTF-8/duplicate-key/schema/loader validation fails |
| `FILE_CHANGE_OPERATION_BINDING_INVALID` | a changed document lacks the required last-change ordering, CLI consumption, or canonical CLI-result projection |
| `FILE_CHANGE_PROJECTION_INVALID` | complete delta partition or behavioral working/support/semantic projection is missing, overlapping, or inconsistent |
| `COMMAND_DECODER_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` | decoder/parser/schema identity drift |
| `COMMAND_DECODER_PARSE_INVALID` | parser error or invalid UTF-16/UTF-8 span |
| `COMMAND_DECODER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | AST/token/depth/statement/operation/pipeline/plan limit |
| `COMMAND_PLAN_SCHEMA_INVALID` | closed decoder-plan schema violation |
| `COMMAND_PLAN_CANONICAL_INVALID` | topology/span/metric/digest/canonical JSON inconsistency |
| `COMMAND_PLAN_RAW_RETAINED_MISMATCH` | sanitized raw and retained normalized plans differ |
| `COMMAND_POLICY_DENIED` | syntax/action/parameter/tool is not in the closed policy |
| `COMMAND_PATH_UNSAFE` | root, ancestry, link, identity, confinement, or race failure |
| `COMMAND_CAPTURE_INVALID` | session root/file identity, event/output span, decoded length/hash, or process-stderr contract failure |
| `COMMAND_OUTPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 64 MiB session, 4 MiB document, or 128-document limit |
| `COMMAND_JSON_INVALID` | malformed/duplicate-key/nonobject/noisy/trailing JSON |
| `COMMAND_JSON_COUNT_MISMATCH` | document count or order differs from operations |
| `COMMAND_RESULT_INCONSISTENT` | exit/success/refusal fields contradict the frozen outcome |
| `COMMAND_ARTIFACT_BINDING_INVALID` | declared output/capture/artifact bytes or hashes mismatch |
| `COMMAND_CONFINEMENT_INVALID` | created/mutated path escapes or inventory differs |
| `COMMAND_FINAL_BINDING_INVALID` | retained final message/session binding fails |

One condition produces one primary code; tests assert the table is complete and
unknown codes cannot serialize. Details are limited to bounded ordinals,
counts, enum labels, and normalized path tokens—never commands, payloads,
private paths, environment values, JSON messages, or provider text.

`reject_existing_archive_output`. All helpers used by positive observations
filter to `outcome="success"`. A valid expected refusal preserves integrity;


The host-review schemas above are recursively closed and canonical in dataclass
order. Candidate `subject_records` is exactly `pre-freeze-gate`,
`candidate-input-aggregate`, `candidate-review-input-bundle`; closure is exactly
`closure-committed-release`, `closure-review-input-bundle`; final-docs is exactly
`final-docs-release`, `final-cumulative-manifest`, `closure-reviewed-release`,
`final-docs-review-input-bundle`. The high-level records retain all prior
recursive bindings. The final subject in each phase is the single content-
complete bundle defined below. Closure release equivalence and final-docs release
equivalence remain their respective `subject_equivalence_sha256` values.
Specification envelopes/results have an empty predecessor array;
quality/security has exactly the same-phase specification PASS result SHA-256.
The six phase/type pairs map one-to-one to the six fixed reviewer task names.

There is no caller-supplied authorized-input manifest, bundle, path, membership,
or hash. The already-authorized `pre-freeze-gate-audit` producer writes exactly
`<phase-root>\host-review-input-bundle.json`; `release-gate-audit` writes the
same fixed leaf inside its existing `closure-committed` or `final-docs` phase
root. No generic root role or eighteenth root authority is added. Each producer
publishes its immutable high-level record first, then creates the bundle leaf
CreateNew so the bundle contains that record without a hash cycle. Neither
artifact constitutes a review input until both revalidate; the envelope derives
separate subject bindings for the record and bundle path/no-follow identity/
size/SHA-256 plus decoded count/bytes/entries aggregate. The bundle is read-only
after publication and any partial, substituted, or obsolete attempt is retain-only.

`HostReviewInputBundle` serializes compact strict UTF-8/LF JSON with top-level
keys exactly `schema_version`, `phase`, `target_head`, `target_tree`,
`target_parent`, `target_base`, `phase_delta_base`, `phase_delta_paths`,
`entries`, `entry_count`, `total_decoded_bytes`, `entries_aggregate_sha256`.
Wrapper-only `canonical_bytes` and `canonical_sha256` are not serialized. Every
entry has keys exactly `path`, `mode`, `blob`, `size`, `sha256`,
`content_base64`; base64 is canonical RFC 4648 with required padding and decodes
to the exact bytes. Repository-entry `mode` is exactly the target-tree mode
`100644` or `100755`; every out-of-tree evidence-entry `mode` is exactly
`100644`, with no `100755` alternative. `blob` is the
lowercase 40-hex Git blob object ID computed over `blob <size>\0<bytes>` even for
out-of-tree evidence. `size` is the decoded byte count and `sha256` is its exact
lowercase digest. `entries_aggregate_sha256` hashes compact LF JSON with the sole
key `entries` and the exact serialized entry array. Entries are strictly sorted
by ordinal UTF-8 `path`, with no duplicate path; phase-set union deduplicates
repository paths by exact path before sorting and never content-deduplicates two
different paths.

For every phase, the repository-entry set is the union of (a) the exact ordered
regular-file change set between fixed base
`30beb3832d18f6d0011bb4f8af96b7cdda9222f6` and `target_head`, (b) the current

anchored source grammar is part of the row, not a discovery pattern. The

not new root roles, authorities, serialized fields, or caller inputs.
