The evidence-entry subsequence is therefore exactly 2, 7, and 9 rows for
candidate, closure, and final-docs. Its set equals the applicable table with no
other `@evidence/` path; its ordinal sequence is respectively `00..01`,
`00..06`, and `00..08`; and each path is the literal concatenation
`@evidence/` + table ordinal + `/` + table role + `/` + table leaf. Every row's
phase, ordinal, role, leaf, path, source artifact, and `100644` mode must match
the same table row. The evidence subsequence remains in table ordinal order,
and the complete repository-plus-evidence `entries` array remains sorted by
ordinal UTF-8 path. Missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, wrong-ordinal,
wrong-role, wrong-leaf, cross-phase, wrong-mode, or source-substituted rows
reject.

The producer selects bytes without a caller choice. Candidate resolves row `00`
from the immutable output it just published and row `01` only from the exact
campaign aggregate binding. Closure resolves row `00` from its immutable output
and rows `01..06` only from the two candidate PASS triplets recursively captured
by that output. Final-docs resolves rows `00..02` from its three high-level
subject bindings and rows `03..08` only from the two closure PASS triplets
recursively captured by `closure-reviewed-release`. For every row it first
matches the table's anchored source grammar and canonical schema/phase/type,
then opens that single named source no-follow, retains the handle, verifies the
bound identity/size/SHA-256, reads those exact bytes once, and revalidates the
same facts through publication. It constructs `path` and `mode` only from the
table and computes `blob`, `size`, `sha256`, and `content_base64` only from the
retained source bytes. It never enumerates a root, chooses a newest artifact,
accepts a source override, or serializes a source path.

`host-review-audit` independently selects the same phase table and reconstructs
the same source bindings from the authenticated high-level records. It reopens
each exact source no-follow and requires table path/mode plus byte-for-byte
content, size, SHA-256, Git blob, and canonical base64 equality for every row;
it then requires exact repository-set union, table evidence-set equality, and
whole-array order. It does not trust a bundle-provided row classification or
source path. Compact strict UTF-8/LF serialization contains no time, GUID,
enumeration order, or process-local value. Consequently identical target-tree,
phase-delta, high-level-subject, and recursively bound review bytes must produce
byte-identical bundle bytes and SHA-256 in separate producer processes.

`phase_delta_base` is fixed base for candidate, the candidate reviewed target
HEAD recursively authenticated by the closure release for closure, and
`target_parent` for final-docs. `phase_delta_paths` is the exact sorted regular-
file delta from that commit to target and must be a subset of repository entries.
Thus closure and final-docs expose both the complete fixed-base target and their
exact phase delta. Repository entry bytes/blob/mode must equal the target-tree
manifest recursively authenticated by the high-level records; evidence bytes
must equal the no-follow captured subjects/triplets. No working-tree or caller
path is an acceptance fact.

Each source/evidence leaf is opened no-follow and its handle-derived length must
be `0..4194304`, within the remaining decoded cap, and within managed-array bounds
before allocation. `entry_count` is `1..8192`, `total_decoded_bytes` is
`1..33554432`, and the encoded bundle leaf is `1..50331648` bytes. Exact and
plus-one tests apply to every cap, including a large sparse or substituted leaf
whose stat exceeds the cap before the first content allocation/read.

The envelope producer derives `HostReviewAuthorizedInputProjection` directly
and only from these phase-fixed `subject_records`. Its entries are byte-for-byte
the same records in order, so counts are exactly 3, 2, and 4. Canonical projection
keys remain `schema_version`, `phase`, `entries`; subject and identity key orders
remain fixed. The envelope publishes projection count/hash plus bundle decoded
entry count/bytes/aggregate; the result copies them, and `host-review-audit`
independently derives and requires equality. A separately supplied projection or
bundle fact rejects.

The subject path grammar is closed to the paths above: the candidate bundle is
`D:\tmp\kokoroarc-c6-task12-prefreeze-<32 lowercase hex>\host-review-input-bundle.json`;
closure and final-docs bundles are the fixed leaf below their respective
`D:\tmp\kokoroarc-c6-task16-(committed|final-docs)-<32 lowercase hex>` roots.
A reviewer may read only its retained envelope, exact high-level subjects (4 MiB
each), and exact bundle (48 MiB), all no-follow, with 64 MiB aggregate read cap.
The exact base64 source/evidence bytes are therefore inspectable without any
repository/worktree authority. It may parse/compare/report bounded findings;
directory enumeration, arbitrary or nested filesystem reads, shell/tool/test
execution, network, credentials, writes, Git mutation, and child-agent spawn are
forbidden. Every registry row and envelope uses literal authority
`retained-envelope-phase-fixed-subjects-and-bundle-bounded-no-follow`.

`host-review-audit` reopens the bundle no-follow, rejects its size before
allocation, and validates every key/type/order/path/mode/blob/size/hash/base64
byte, entry order, deduplication, aggregate/count/cap, phase delta, mandatory
current documents/campaign/source/schema/test set, fixed-base target change set,
and recursively bound evidence set against the target-tree and subject manifests.
Substitution, omission, addition, reorder, stale bytes, over-cap content, or a
bundle field not identical across envelope/result/audit rejects before audit
publication.

Every subject record has exactly `role,path,identity,size,sha256`; identity has
exactly `device,inode,file_type,reparse_tag,link_count`. Every finding has exactly
`severity,line_start,line_end,quoted_text,why_blocking,minimal_correction`.
There are at most 64 findings per array; quoted text is at most 4,096 UTF-8
bytes, each explanatory field at most 8,192 bytes, and line numbers are positive
with `line_end >= line_start`. A PASS has both arrays empty; BLOCKED has at least
one finding, with severity equal to its containing array. The envelope cap is
131,072 bytes and result cap is 262,144 bytes. Unknown, duplicate, missing,
reordered, null, over-cap, cross-phase, or wrong-typed content rejects.

The displayed `materialize_spawn_environment` signature is a broker-local API
implemented only inside the authenticated Task 9 Python bootstrap. It is not
defined, exported, or importable from a repository role module. A guarded
client-preflight or execute target may build and freeze only the canonical
secret-free `ClientLaunchSpec` and, where required, its byte-backed
`ApprovedClientLaunchEvidence`; it sends those canonical bytes through the
authenticated broker request. The trusted root reopens them with its stdlib-
only parser and alone calls the broker-local materializer immediately before
`CreateProcessW`. Synthetic tests exercise that implementation through a
trusted broker harness, never by granting a guarded target the callable.

`validate_execute_preack_stdlib` lives in the committed Task 9 bootstrap and
uses only already imported stdlib modules plus descriptor-opened byte buffers.
It performs strict duplicate-key JSON decoding, exact canonical-byte/hash/
schema checks, and no-follow absence-snapshot validation; it imports no Task 10
or repository module and exposes no filesystem, process, socket, credential, or
mutation callback. It binds the constructor class/table digest and exact
preclaim facts into `ExecutePreAckReceipt`. Missing, malformed, duplicate,
replayed, noncanonical, wrong-nonce/hash/role, or present marker/terminal/root/
claim input rejects before ACK. The receipt is bootstrap evidence only and
cannot authorize either execute transition; after its authenticated GO the
restricted execute target imports Task 10 and must freshly call
`validate_provider_execution_authorization` before any marker, claim,
capability, secret-pipe, credential, or descendant action.

`ProviderExecutionAuthorization.canonical_bytes` is one compact strict-ASCII
JSON object followed by exactly one LF. Serialized keys occur exactly in this
order:
`schema_version`, `approved_campaign_sha256`, `approval_envelope_sha256`,
`approval_prompt_sha256`, `provider_approval_sha256`, `reservation_sha256`,
`preclaim_snapshot_sha256`, `credential_transport_version`,
`credential_environment_name`. The schema value is
`complete-suite-provider-execution-authorization-v1`; the transport and name
are exactly `complete-suite-provider-credential-pipe-v1` and
`OPENAI_API_KEY`. `canonical_bytes` and `canonical_sha256` are wrapper fields,
not serialized fields. No path, timestamp, nonce, random value, error text, or
credential is permitted.

Task 9's private
`reconstruct_provider_execution_authorization_stdlib` receives only the
authenticated root descriptor plus descriptor-opened campaign, approval-
envelope, prompt, provider-record, reservation, and retained pre-ACK snapshot
bytes. It derives expected hashes and both credential literals from that
descriptor, independently strict-parses and revalidates every cross-binding,
and emits exactly the canonical bytes above. It accepts no callback, repository
object, path, or caller-provided expected field.

`validate_execute_claim_capability_stdlib` also lives in that locked Task 9
broker module. It accepts only descriptor-opened bytes, performs the same strict
canonical/no-follow checks, derives every path from the authenticated root
descriptor rather than the capability. It receives no Task 10 authorization
object or caller-supplied authorization bytes. Instead it retains the exact
pre-ACK snapshot bytes in broker memory, reopens the descriptor-bound campaign,
approval envelope, approval prompt, provider record, reservation, execute-
consumption marker, claim, raw-root snapshot, and candidate-input aggregate,
and runs a separately reviewed stdlib-only reconstruction of the canonical
detached authorization. Differential tests require that reconstruction's bytes
and SHA-256 to equal Task 10's `validate_provider_execution_authorization`
result for every accepted and rejected vector and for mutation of every ordered
key. It compares the reconstructed canonical hash, its six constituent hash
fields, and the two credential-literal fields to both the capability and
authenticated descriptors,
then proves exact agreement among that authorization, reservation,
marker, claim, raw-root identity/membership, candidate-input aggregate, frozen
client identity, launch-template digest, constructor digests, and root/target
PID/creation-time bindings. It accepts exactly one canonical
`ExecuteClaimCapability` from the authenticated execute root-role target and
returns no repository object or credential-bearing value. Any mismatch rejects
before secret-pipe creation and with credential lookup/transfer counters still
zero; no durable authorization file or hidden target-to-root byte channel is
required.

Capture the native installed Codex executable path/hash/version closure; absolute
`pwsh.exe` path, file SHA-256, file version, product version, `PSEdition`,
`PSVersion`, and parser assembly version; and the exact `rg` and Python
identities. The PowerShell probe itself uses `-NoLogo -NoProfile
-NonInteractive`. Repeat the shell-renderer part twice and require identical
normalized facts and rendered shell-event bytes. The evaluator model identity is
exactly `gpt-5.6-terra` in loopback and real projections; it is not normalizable
because the installed client may derive its tool advertisement from model
capabilities.

The Codex version check is process-free. Capture the main `@openai/codex`
`package.json` and the `@openai/codex-win32-x64` platform `package.json` through
explicit paths supplied to the producer. Strict duplicate-key JSON decoding must
prove the main package name/version are exactly `@openai/codex`/`0.149.0`, its
`bin.codex` and Windows-x64 optional-dependency selector are exact, the platform
manifest is exactly the Windows-x64 `0.149.0-win32-x64` package, and the native
`codex.exe` is the exact plain regular member at the frozen platform-relative
path. Bind both manifests' paths, identities, sizes, exact bytes and SHA-256,
the executable identity/size/hash, their no-follow ancestor relationship, and
the derived literal label `codex-cli 0.149.0` in one
`FrozenCodexClientIdentity`. `validate_frozen_codex_client_identity` only
reopens and rechecks those approval-bound records; it never invokes Codex,
Node, a package manager, a shell, or a version command. The four enveloped live
probes below must all start that same recaptured native executable identity and
thereby bind the working renderer to this distribution closure.

The producer does not trust runbook discovery. It independently no-follow-opens
every executable and requires the caller's Codex and `rg` paths to be the exact
members below the two validated package manifests, the shell to equal the
plan-pinned `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe` size/hash/product/file-
version tuple, and Python to equal the plan-pinned
`C:\Python314\python.exe` tuple. The two scalar runbooks derive Codex/`rg` from
the literal `D:\DevLanguages\nodejs\node_global` package root and never invoke
or resolve the `codex` shim. Any alternate, duplicate, PATH-only, alias,
function, script, reparse, hardlink among those four inputs, changed, or unlocked
input rejects before the shell, Codex, or another child can start. Git and Node
use the distinct closed hardlink rules immediately below.

The preflight also captures exactly two process-free `FrozenNativeLeaf`
records, ordered `git` then `node`, from the caller-supplied absolute native
Git-for-Windows `Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\git.exe` and native
`Program Files\nodejs\node.exe` paths. These locations are derived only from the
Windows known-folder API; PATH, the small `cmd\git.exe` launcher, and a user
version-manager directory are never discovery inputs or broker targets. Bind
each no-follow executable and ancestor
identity, size, SHA-256, Windows file/product version, role, and ordered
aggregate hash. Process-free `FindFirstFileNameW`/`FindNextFileNameW`
enumeration must prove Node has the singleton hardlink set containing only its
own path. The standard Git-for-Windows main binary must have exactly this
sorted same-volume four-path hardlink set, with one shared file identity and
bytes, and no other link:

```text
\Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\git-receive-pack.exe
\Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\git-upload-archive.exe
\Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\git-upload-pack.exe
\Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\git.exe
```

Only the literal `git.exe` path is launchable; the three server aliases remain
nonlaunchable identities and a request naming one rejects. Reject an alternate,
duplicate, PATH-only, shim/script, unexpected/additional/relocated hardlink,
reparse, changed, or non-PE input. Neither capture nor validation executes a
version/help command. Task 10's broker may launch only these exact
recaptured identities for its closed Git and Node leaf grammars; later campaign
and release records bind their aggregate without rediscovery.
The Git leaf record's permitted constructor tuple is exactly host then broker,
with each implementation body hash; Node and `powershell_decoder` each permit
only broker. Every concrete descriptor/precreation/process record selects
exactly one context-valid tuple member and repeats its ID/hash. The frozen leaf
record never lets a caller select or add an implementation.
The producer independently resolves both known-folder descendants with Windows
no-follow handle APIs and requires the caller paths to match; the runbook's
known-folder resolution is not trusted as its own proof.

After the separately approved `worktree add`, Step 6 uses a new non-escalated
PowerShell process whose short fixed bootstrap contains no Task 9 or request
source bytes. The independently audited bootstrap literals bind the producer
blob/size/SHA-256, while the separately authenticated handoff supplies an
independent copy of the complete producer tuple; disagreement rejects. The
bootstrap retains and executes the exact prior-checkpoint source as described
above. The producer constructs one in-memory ordered `$Task9TransitionInputs`
object; it is never read from caller JSON or Task 9 repository code. The source-
only script below accepts exactly the
keys it names. `checkout_entries` is the already validated, ordinal, exhaustive
`ls-tree`/checkout projection held in producer memory, with every `size`
explicitly typed `[long]`. Before constructing the object, the plan-owned script
opens the committed control-plane, Python bootstrap, artifact launcher, and
artifact-writer blobs as bounded
strict UTF-8 data,
extracts the four uniquely delimited canonical JSON literals for the four-entry
selection registry, two-entry constructor-implementation registry, and
three-entry constructor-class registry and seven-row Job-topology registry
without evaluating PowerShell/Python,
extracts both delimited implementation source bodies plus the artifact TTY
contract literal, and requires the two body hashes and five registry/contract
hashes to equal the independently fixed non-artifact plan bindings. It separately
requires the artifact-launcher and artifact-writer source tuples and the six
artifact semantic projections to equal both the independently reviewed `H`/`O`
chain and the projections recomputed from the exact Task 9 checkout bytes; Task 9
test literals are never the expected side of that comparison. It also constructs the four literal expected selection records below in
memory and requires canonical semantic equality with the extracted selection
registry; IDs and ordered top-level keys alone are insufficient.
The exact delimiter lines are
`# C6-POST-TRUST-SELECTION-REGISTRY-BEGIN`/`# C6-POST-TRUST-SELECTION-REGISTRY-END`
and `# C6-CONSTRUCTOR-IMPLEMENTATION-SET-BEGIN`/
`# C6-CONSTRUCTOR-IMPLEMENTATION-SET-END`
and `# C6-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-SET-BEGIN`/`# C6-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-SET-END`
and `# C6-JOB-TOPOLOGY-BEGIN`/`# C6-JOB-TOPOLOGY-END`, while the launcher uses
`# C6-ARTIFACT-TTY-CONTRACT-BEGIN`/`# C6-ARTIFACT-TTY-CONTRACT-END` around one
canonical compact ASCII JSON line.
Independently, both artifact source files contain exactly one adjacent three-
line source-oracle marker:
`# C6-ARTIFACT-SOURCE-ORACLE-BEGIN`, then
`# C6-ARTIFACT-SOURCE-ORACLE <canonical compact ASCII JSON>`, then
`# C6-ARTIFACT-SOURCE-ORACLE-END`. The launcher object's ordered keys are
`launcher_ast_sha256`, `launcher_bootstrap_fixture_sha256`,
`launcher_rawui_reader_sha256`; the writer object's ordered keys are
`writer_ast_sha256`, `writer_closed_import_native_call_table_sha256`,
`writer_launcher_fixture_sha256`. Each value is 64 lowercase hex. The marker is
only a deterministic projection carrier: its values must equal both the
independent H/O review and recomputation from the exact source/fixture bytes, so
it cannot attest itself.
Each pair occurs once and encloses exactly a PowerShell single-quoted here-string
assignment named `$script:C6PostTrustSelectionRegistryJson`,
`$script:C6ConstructorImplementationSetJson`,
`$script:C6ConstructorAttributeSetJson`, or `$script:C6JobTopologyJson`,
respectively, with exactly one compact
ASCII JSON payload line. The hash is over that payload line without the
assignment, delimiters, or LF. Duplicate delimiters, blank/intervening payload
lines, alternate assignment grammar, noncanonical bytes, or a semantic mismatch
with the closed tables rejects the transition.
After those checks, `Get-C6Task9TransitionInputs` places the five independently
computed payload digests and the two independently computed implementation-body
digests directly into its returned ordered object. No caller supplies those
fields and no registry digest is copied from a field inside its own payload.
The implementation-set JSON contains exactly the two ordered IDs, exact source-
body hashes, exact source-relative paths, and exact permitted contexts. Its
body hashes must equal independent extraction from the PowerShell and Python
files, preventing a registry-only substitution. Those six 64-hex values are
closed producer outputs, not scalar inputs. No source body, checkout inventory,
artifact request, or thousands-entry serialization enters an argv.

The executable bootstrap is the separately audited short fixture
`complete-suite-task9-transition-bootstrap-v1`. Its exact serializer must remain
within the 30,000-unit command budget at maximum paths, and its one-unit-over RED
must fail before `exec_command`. Its complete implementation uses only .NET APIs
to authenticate/strict-parse the handoff, validate the producer tuple, retain the
source handle, validate the compact handoff and multi-line LF source with their
distinct byte-envelope validators, decode the exact retained bytes, create the
ScriptBlock, invoke
the eight arguments below synchronously in the same fresh outer process, rehash
the same handle, require exactly one bounded canonical result line and no error,
and let that outer request return exit zero. The producer's individually bounded
Git children retain their own deadline/kill-tree rules; no separate producer
process, independently killable in-process ScriptBlock, or second runspace is
claimed. This security-significant shape contains no source body or repository
lookup:

~~~powershell
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
$handoffPath='<HANDOFF_PATH>'
$handoffSha256='<HANDOFF_SHA256>'
$task8Commit='<TASK8_COMMIT>'
$task9Commit='<TASK9_COMMIT>'
$checkoutRoot='<CHECKOUT_ROOT>'
$artifactOracleHandoffPath='<ORACLE_HANDOFF_PATH>'
$artifactOracleHandoffSha256='<ORACLE_HANDOFF_SHA256>'
$artifactOracleCheckoutRoot='<ORACLE_CHECKOUT_ROOT>'
$oracleCommit='<ORACLE_COMMIT>'
$oracleParent='<ORACLE_PARENT>'
$producerRelative='docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-kokoroarc-complete-suite-campaign-6-task9-transition.ps1'
$oracleRelative='docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-kokoroarc-complete-suite-campaign-6-task9-artifact-source-oracle.json'
$producerBlob='<PRODUCER_BLOB>'
$producerSize=[long]::Parse(
    '<PRODUCER_SIZE>',
    [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture
)
$producerSha256='<PRODUCER_SHA256>'

function Read-C6BootstrapStream {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][IO.FileStream]$Stream,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][long]$MaxBytes,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label
    )
    if (-not $Stream.CanRead -or -not $Stream.CanSeek -or $Stream.Length -lt 2 -or
        $Stream.Length -gt $MaxBytes -or $Stream.Length -gt [int]::MaxValue) {
        throw "$Label stream envelope"
    }
    $Stream.Position=0
    [byte[]]$bytes=[byte[]]::new([int]$Stream.Length)
    $offset=0
    while ($offset -lt $bytes.Length) {
        $count=$Stream.Read($bytes,$offset,$bytes.Length-$offset)
        if ($count -le 0) {throw "$Label short read"}
        $offset += $count
    }
    if ($Stream.ReadByte() -ne -1) {throw "$Label grew"}
    return ,$bytes
}

function Assert-C6BootstrapTextEnvelope {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][byte[]]$Bytes,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][bool]$InternalLfAllowed
    )
    if ($Bytes.Length -lt 2 -or $Bytes[-1] -ne 10 -or
        ($Bytes.Length -ge 3 -and $Bytes[0] -eq 239 -and
         $Bytes[1] -eq 187 -and $Bytes[2] -eq 191)) {
        throw "$Label text envelope"
    }
    for ($index=0; $index -lt $Bytes.Length; $index++) {
        if ($Bytes[$index] -eq 0 -or $Bytes[$index] -eq 13 -or
            (-not $InternalLfAllowed -and $Bytes[$index] -eq 10 -and
             $index -ne $Bytes.Length-1)) {
            throw "$Label text envelope"
        }
    }
}

function Assert-C6BootstrapCompactJsonBytes {
    param([byte[]]$Bytes,[string]$Label)
    Assert-C6BootstrapTextEnvelope $Bytes $Label $false
}

function Assert-C6BootstrapLfSourceBytes {
    param([byte[]]$Bytes,[string]$Label)
    Assert-C6BootstrapTextEnvelope $Bytes $Label $true
}

function Get-C6BootstrapSha256 {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][byte[]]$Bytes)
    return [Convert]::ToHexString(
        [Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::HashData($Bytes)
    ).ToLowerInvariant()
}

function Get-C6BootstrapGitBlob {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][byte[]]$Bytes)
    $hash=[Security.Cryptography.IncrementalHash]::CreateHash(
        [Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName]::SHA1
    )
    try {
        $header=[Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes(
            'blob ' + $Bytes.Length + [char]0
        )
        $hash.AppendData($header)
        $hash.AppendData($Bytes)
        return [Convert]::ToHexString($hash.GetHashAndReset()).ToLowerInvariant()
    } finally { $hash.Dispose() }
}

function Get-C6BootstrapStreamSha256 {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][IO.FileStream]$Stream,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][long]$ExpectedLength,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label
    )
    if ($Stream.Length -ne $ExpectedLength) {throw "$Label length drift"}
    $Stream.Position=0
    $hash=[Security.Cryptography.IncrementalHash]::CreateHash(
        [Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName]::SHA256
    )
    try {
        $buffer=[byte[]]::new(65536)
        [long]$total=0
        while (($count=$Stream.Read($buffer,0,$buffer.Length)) -gt 0) {
            $total += $count
            if ($total -gt $ExpectedLength) {throw "$Label grew"}
            $hash.AppendData($buffer,0,$count)
        }
        if ($total -ne $ExpectedLength) {throw "$Label truncated"}
        [Convert]::ToHexString($hash.GetHashAndReset()).ToLowerInvariant()
    } finally {$hash.Dispose()}
}

function Assert-C6BootstrapObject {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][Text.Json.JsonElement]$Element,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$ExpectedNames,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$ExpectedKinds,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label
    )
    if ($Element.ValueKind -ne [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::Object -or
        $ExpectedNames.Count -ne $ExpectedKinds.Count) {throw "$Label schema"}
    $p=[Collections.Generic.List[Text.Json.JsonProperty]]::new()
    $e=$Element.EnumerateObject()
    while ($e.MoveNext()) {[void]$p.Add($e.Current)}
    if ($p.Count -ne $ExpectedNames.Count) {throw "$Label count"}
    for ($index=0; $index -lt $ExpectedNames.Count; $index++) {
        if ($p[$index].Name -cne $ExpectedNames[$index] -or
            ([string]$p[$index].Value.ValueKind) -cne
                $ExpectedKinds[$index]) {
            throw "$Label property $index"
        }
    }
    return ,$p.ToArray()
}

function Get-C6BootstrapArray {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][Text.Json.JsonElement]$Element,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][int]$ExpectedCount,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label
    )
    if ($Element.ValueKind -ne [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::Array) {throw "$Label type"}
    $a=[Collections.Generic.List[Text.Json.JsonElement]]::new()
    $e=$Element.EnumerateArray()
    while ($e.MoveNext()) {[void]$a.Add($e.Current)}
    if ($a.Count -ne $ExpectedCount) {throw "$Label count"}
    return ,$a.ToArray()
}

function Assert-C6BootstrapScalars {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][Text.Json.JsonProperty[]]$Properties,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][int[]]$StringIndexes,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][int[]]$IntegerIndexes,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label
    )
    foreach ($index in $StringIndexes) {
        $value=$Properties[$index].Value.GetString()
        if ($null -eq $value -or $value.Length -gt 1048576 -or
            $value.IndexOf([char]0) -ge 0) {
            throw "$Label string $index"
        }
    }
    foreach ($index in $IntegerIndexes) {
        [long]$value=0
        if (-not $Properties[$index].Value.TryGetInt64([ref]$value) -or
            $value -lt 0) {
            throw "$Label integer $index"
        }
    }
}

function Assert-C6BootstrapNativeString {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowNull()][object]$Value)
    if ($null -eq $Value -or $Value -isnot [string]) {throw 'native string type'}
    [string]$text=$Value
    for ($index=0; $index -lt $text.Length; $index++) {
        $character=$text[$index]
        if ($character -eq [char]0) {throw 'native NUL'}
        if ([char]::IsHighSurrogate($character)) {
            if ($index+1 -ge $text.Length -or
                -not [char]::IsLowSurrogate($text[$index+1])) {
                throw 'native surrogate'
            }
            $index++
        } elseif ([char]::IsLowSurrogate($character)) {
            throw 'native surrogate'
        }
    }
}

function ConvertTo-C6BootstrapNativeArgument {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowNull()][object]$Value)
    Assert-C6BootstrapNativeString $Value
    [string]$text=$Value
    $quoted=($text.Length -eq 0 -or $text.IndexOfAny([char[]]@('"',' ',[char]9)) -ge 0)
    if (-not $quoted) { return $text }
    $builder=[Text.StringBuilder]::new()
    [void]$builder.Append('"')
    $slashes=0
    foreach ($character in $text.ToCharArray()) {
        if ($character -eq '\') { $slashes++; continue }
        if ($character -eq '"') {
            if ($slashes) {[void]$builder.Append(('\'*(2*$slashes)))}
            [void]$builder.Append('\"')
            $slashes=0
            continue
        }
        if ($slashes) {[void]$builder.Append(('\'*$slashes));$slashes=0}
        [void]$builder.Append($character)
    }
    if ($slashes) {[void]$builder.Append(('\'*(2*$slashes)))}
    [void]$builder.Append('"')
    return $builder.ToString()
}

function Get-C6BootstrapNativeBinding {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowNull()][object]$Executable,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowNull()][object]$Arguments
    )
    Assert-C6BootstrapNativeString $Executable
    [string]$executableText=$Executable
    if (-not [IO.Path]::IsPathFullyQualified($executableText)) {throw 'native exe'}
    if ($null -eq $Arguments -or $Arguments -isnot [object[]]) {
        throw 'native argv type'
    }
    $parts=[Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
    [void]$parts.Add((ConvertTo-C6BootstrapNativeArgument $executableText))
    foreach ($argument in [object[]]$Arguments) {
        [void]$parts.Add((ConvertTo-C6BootstrapNativeArgument $argument))
    }
    $commandLine=[string]::Join(' ',$parts)
    [long]$units=$commandLine.Length+1
    if ($units -gt 30000) {throw 'native vector budget'}
    $bytes=[Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($commandLine+[char]0)
    $digest=[Convert]::ToHexString(
        [Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::HashData($bytes)
    ).ToLowerInvariant()
    return [Tuple[long,string]]::new($units,$digest)
}

function Get-C6BootstrapGitTail {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Role,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$PlanCommit,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$PlanParent,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Task9Commit,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$OracleCommit,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$OracleParent
    )
    switch -CaseSensitive ($Role) {
        'source-root' {@('rev-parse','--show-toplevel');break}
        {$_ -in @('source-head','checkout-head','oracle-head')} {@('rev-parse','--verify','HEAD^{commit}');break}
        {$_ -in @('source-tree','checkout-tree','oracle-tree')} {@('rev-parse','--verify','HEAD^{tree}');break}
        {$_ -in @('source-parent','oracle-parent')} {@('rev-parse','--verify','HEAD^1');break}
        {$_ -in @('source-parent-line','oracle-parent-line')} {@('rev-list','--parents','-n','1','HEAD');break}
        {$_ -in @('source-subject','oracle-subject')} {@('show','-s','--format=%s','HEAD');break}
        'source-branch' {@('symbolic-ref','--short','HEAD');break}
        {$_ -in @('source-status','checkout-status','oracle-status')} {@('status','--porcelain=v2','--untracked-files=all');break}
        'plan-tree' {@('rev-parse','--verify',"$PlanCommit`^{tree}");break}
        'plan-parent' {@('rev-parse','--verify',"$PlanCommit`^1");break}
        'plan-message' {@('show','-s','--format=%B',$PlanCommit);break}
        'plan-entries' {@('ls-tree','-z',$PlanCommit,'--',$producerRelative,'docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-kokoroarc-complete-suite-campaign-6.md');break}
        'plan-delta' {@('diff-tree','--no-commit-id','--name-status','-z','-r',$PlanParent,$PlanCommit,'--');break}
        'plan-ancestor' {@('merge-base','--is-ancestor',$PlanCommit,$Task9Commit);break}
        {$_ -in @('checkout-detached','oracle-detached')} {@('symbolic-ref','-q','HEAD');break}
        'checkout-ls-tree' {@('ls-tree','-r','-z','-l','--full-tree',$Task9Commit);break}
        'oracle-entries' {@('ls-tree','-z',$OracleCommit,'--',$oracleRelative);break}
        'oracle-delta' {@('diff-tree','--no-commit-id','--name-status','-z','-r',$OracleParent,$OracleCommit,'--');break}
        default {throw "unregistered Git role: $Role"}
    }
}

    for ($index=0; $index -lt $bindingItems.Count; $index++) {

        } elseif ($role.StartsWith(
                'oracle-',[StringComparison]::Ordinal)) {

        } else { $sourceRoot }
        $tail=@(Get-C6BootstrapGitTail $role $planCommit $planParent `

        $native=Get-C6BootstrapNativeBinding -Executable $git `

    }
    if ((Get-C6BootstrapStreamSha256 $producerStream $producerSize producer) -cne

        (Get-C6BootstrapStreamSha256 $handoffStream $handoffBytes.Length handoff) -cne

        (Get-C6BootstrapStreamSha256 $artifactOracleHandoffStream `

        ([IO.File]::GetAttributes($producerPath) -band
            [IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) -ne 0) {

    }
    [Console]::Out.WriteLine($resultLine)

    if ($handoffDocument) { $handoffDocument.Dispose() }
~~~

The fence above is the complete executable fixture; no prose continuation is
required. With its LF terminator it is 29,185 UTF-16 code units before literal
substitution. The canonical maximum-vector fixture uses, in placeholder order,
a 32-`0` plan-handoff GUID suffix; 64 `1` handoff-SHA digits; 40 `2` Task 8 and
40 `3` Task 9 commit digits; a 32-`4` checkout GUID suffix; a 32-`5` oracle-
handoff GUID suffix; 64 `6` oracle-handoff-SHA digits; a 32-`7` oracle-checkout
GUID suffix; 40 `8` oracle-commit and 40 `9` oracle-parent digits; 40 `a`
producer-blob digits; producer size `1048576`; and 64 `b` producer-SHA digits.
These are repetitions of the shown lowercase hexadecimal digit. They produce
the maximum legal plan handoff path (70), detached checkout root (68), oracle
handoff path (94), oracle checkout root (90), five OIDs/commits (40 each), three
SHA-256 values (64 each), and producer decimal size (7). Replacing all 13
placeholders adds exactly 505 units for a 29,690-unit body. The observed 72-unit
tool prefix makes the `-Command` payload 29,762 units. Applying
the frozen Windows quoting serializer to absolute
`C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`, `-NoProfile`, `-Command`, and that
payload, with separators and terminal NUL, yields exactly 29,876 UTF-16 units and
UTF-16LE SHA-256
`212df21dca0c9cdd3f2f9888acbe15bbac54ed667f79586f714f4933b462ab4c`:
124 units below the 30,000 contract. The exact-at fixture adds exactly 124
bounded inert safe units after the end marker to reach 30,000; adding 125 reaches
30,001 and
must reject before `exec_command`, source open, or transition output.

The next fence is source-only and is materialized byte-for-byte as the
prior-checkpoint script; it is never an inline tool command. Its early
`SuccessorVerifierSource` branch returns exactly one 39,689-byte strict-LF
string with SHA-256
`a84d12d48b95b820c2bbbbc301879cb90bb30aac6203a6cd3368c19fff78719c`.
That digest is frozen independently in this audited plan, not learned from the
runtime output.

~~~powershell
[CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName='Transition')]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory,ParameterSetName='Transition',Position=0)]
    [string]$HandoffPath,

    [ValidatePattern('^[0-9a-f]{64}$')]
    [string]$ExpectedHandoffSha256,

function Read-C6AuthenticatedBytes {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [ValidatePattern('^[0-9a-f]{64}$')][string]$Sha256,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [ValidateSet(
            'receipt','trust','transition','oracle','zero-envelope','manifest',
            'control-plane','bootstrap','launcher','writer','host-review-result'
        )]
        [string]$Role
    )
    [long]$cap=switch ($Role) {
        'zero-envelope' { 16384L }
        'host-review-result' { 262144L }
        'manifest' { 8388608L }
        'control-plane' { 4194304L }
        'bootstrap' { 4194304L }
        'launcher' { 1048576L }
        'writer' { 1048576L }
        default { 65536L }
    }
    if (-not [IO.Path]::IsPathFullyQualified($Path)) {
        throw "authenticated path is not absolute: $Path"
    }
    $item=Get-Item -LiteralPath $Path -Force -ErrorAction Stop
    if ($item.PSIsContainer -or
        (($item.Attributes -band [IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) -ne 0)) {
        throw "authenticated path is not an observed plain file: $Path"
    }
    $stream=$null
    try {
        $stream=[IO.FileStream]::new(
            $item.FullName,[IO.FileMode]::Open,[IO.FileAccess]::Read,
            [IO.FileShare]::Read,65536,[IO.FileOptions]::SequentialScan
        )
        if ($stream.Length -lt 1 -or $stream.Length -gt $cap -or
            $stream.Length -gt [int]::MaxValue -or
            $stream.Length -ne $item.Length) {
            throw "authenticated role/length mismatch: $Role"
        }
        [byte[]]$bytes=[byte[]]::new([int]$stream.Length)
        $offset=0
        while ($offset -lt $bytes.Length) {
            $count=$stream.Read($bytes,$offset,$bytes.Length-$offset)
            if ($count -le 0) { throw "authenticated short read: $Role" }
            $offset += $count
        }
        if ($stream.ReadByte() -ne -1 -or $stream.Length -ne $bytes.Length) {
            throw "authenticated retained-stream drift: $Role"
        }
        $actual=[Convert]::ToHexString(
            [Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::HashData($bytes)
        ).ToLowerInvariant()
        if ($actual -cne $Sha256) {
            throw "authenticated byte hash mismatch: $Role"
        }
        return [pscustomobject]@{
            role=$Role; path=$item.FullName; sha256=$Sha256
            length=[long]$bytes.Length; bytes=$bytes; stream=$stream
        }
    } catch {
        if ($null -ne $stream) { $stream.Dispose() }
        throw
    }
}

function Confirm-C6AuthenticatedBytes {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)]$Held)
    if ($Held.stream.Length -ne $Held.length) {
        throw "authenticated retained length drift: $($Held.role)"
    }
    $Held.stream.Position=0
    $hasher=[Security.Cryptography.IncrementalHash]::CreateHash(
        [Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName]::SHA256
    )
    try {
        $buffer=[byte[]]::new(65536)
        [long]$total=0
        while (($count=$Held.stream.Read($buffer,0,$buffer.Length)) -gt 0) {
            $total += $count
            if ($total -gt $Held.length) {
                throw "authenticated retained stream grew: $($Held.role)"
            }
            $hasher.AppendData($buffer,0,$count)
        }
        $actual=[Convert]::ToHexString(
            $hasher.GetHashAndReset()
        ).ToLowerInvariant()
        if ($total -ne $Held.length -or $actual -cne $Held.sha256) {
            throw "authenticated retained rehash mismatch: $($Held.role)"
        }
    } finally { $hasher.Dispose() }
}

function ConvertFrom-C6AuthenticatedJson {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]$Held,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$ExpectedKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$IntegerKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$BooleanKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$ObjectKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$ArrayKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label
    )
    $encoding=[Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false,$true)
    $text=$encoding.GetString($Held.bytes)
    if (-not $text.EndsWith("`n") -or $text.Contains("`r") -or
        $text.Contains([char]0)) { throw "$Label text envelope" }
    $options=[Text.Json.JsonDocumentOptions]::new()
    $options.AllowTrailingCommas=$false
    $options.CommentHandling=[Text.Json.JsonCommentHandling]::Disallow
    $options.MaxDepth=32
    $document=[Text.Json.JsonDocument]::Parse(
        [ReadOnlyMemory[byte]]::new($Held.bytes),$options
    )
    try {
        if ($document.RootElement.ValueKind -ne
                [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::Object -or
            $document.RootElement.GetRawText() -cne
                $text.Substring(0,$text.Length-1)) {
            throw "$Label JSON root/framing"
        }
        $properties=[Collections.Generic.List[Text.Json.JsonProperty]]::new()
        $enumerator=$document.RootElement.EnumerateObject()
        while ($enumerator.MoveNext()) { [void]$properties.Add($enumerator.Current) }
        if ($properties.Count -ne $ExpectedKeys.Count) {
            throw "$Label JSON property count"
        }
        for ($index=0; $index -lt $ExpectedKeys.Count; $index++) {
            $property=$properties[$index]
            $name=$property.Name
            $expectedKind=if ($IntegerKeys -ccontains $name) {
                [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::Number
            } elseif ($BooleanKeys -ccontains $name) {
                if ($property.Value.GetBoolean()) {
                    [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::True
                } else { [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::False }
            } elseif ($ObjectKeys -ccontains $name) {
                [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::Object
            } elseif ($ArrayKeys -ccontains $name) {
                [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::Array
            } else { [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::String }
            if ($name -cne $ExpectedKeys[$index] -or
                $property.Value.ValueKind -ne $expectedKind) {
                throw "$Label JSON name/type: $index"
            }
            if ($IntegerKeys -ccontains $name) {
                [long]$number=0
                if (-not $property.Value.TryGetInt64([ref]$number)) {
                    throw "$Label JSON integer: $name"
                }
            } elseif ($expectedKind -eq [Text.Json.JsonValueKind]::String -and
                $null -eq $property.Value.GetString()) {
                throw "$Label JSON null string: $name"
            }
        }
    } finally { $document.Dispose() }
    $value=$text | ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable -NoEnumerate -ErrorAction Stop
    if ($value -isnot [Collections.IDictionary] -or
        (@($value.Keys) -join "`n") -cne ($ExpectedKeys -join "`n") -or
        (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $value -Compress -Depth 30) + "`n" -cne
            $text) {
        throw "$Label PowerShell/canonical mismatch"
    }
    foreach ($key in $ExpectedKeys) {
        if ($IntegerKeys -ccontains $key) {
            if ($value[$key] -isnot [long]) { throw "$Label integer: $key" }
        } elseif ($BooleanKeys -ccontains $key) {
            if ($value[$key] -isnot [bool]) { throw "$Label boolean: $key" }
        } elseif ($ObjectKeys -ccontains $key) {
            if ($value[$key] -isnot [Collections.IDictionary]) {
                throw "$Label object: $key"
            }
        } elseif ($ArrayKeys -ccontains $key) {
            if ($value[$key] -isnot [object[]]) { throw "$Label array: $key" }
        } elseif ($value[$key] -isnot [string]) {
            throw "$Label string: $key"
        }
    }
    return $value
}

function Assert-C6AuthenticatedObject {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]$Value,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$ExpectedKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label
    )
    if ($Value -isnot [Collections.IDictionary] -or
        (@($Value.Keys) -join "`n") -cne ($ExpectedKeys -join "`n")) {
        throw "$Label object/key order"
    }
}

function Assert-C6AuthenticatedScalarTypes {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][Collections.IDictionary]$Value,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$StringKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$IntegerKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string[]]$BooleanKeys,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Label
    )
    foreach ($key in $StringKeys) {
        if ($Value[$key] -isnot [string]) { throw "$Label string: $key" }
    }
    foreach ($key in $IntegerKeys) {
        if ($Value[$key] -isnot [long]) { throw "$Label integer: $key" }
    }
    foreach ($key in $BooleanKeys) {
        if ($Value[$key] -isnot [bool]) { throw "$Label boolean: $key" }
    }
}

function Get-C6AuthenticatedGitBlob {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][byte[]]$Bytes)
    $hasher=[Security.Cryptography.IncrementalHash]::CreateHash(
        [Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName]::SHA1
    )
    try {
        $header=[Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes(
            'blob ' + $Bytes.LongLength + [char]0
        )
        $hasher.AppendData($header)
        $hasher.AppendData($Bytes)
        return [Convert]::ToHexString(
            $hasher.GetHashAndReset()
        ).ToLowerInvariant()
    } finally { $hasher.Dispose() }
}
~~~
