~~~powershell
            pytest_argv=$task10Argv
            binding_keys=[ordered]@{
                'authenticated-provisional'=[object[]]@(
                    'source_root','source_identity_mode','selection',
                    'guard_source','guard_record',
                    'expected_guard_record_sha256','phase_root',
                    'expected_parent','expected_tree','provisional_record',
                    'expected_provisional_record_sha256','output',
                    'evaluation_envelope_record','evaluation_envelope_sha256'
                )
                commit=[object[]]@(
                    'source_root','source_identity_mode','selection',
                    'guard_source','guard_record',
                    'expected_guard_record_sha256','phase_root','expected_head',
                    'expected_parent','expected_tree','prior_audit_record',
                    'expected_prior_audit_record_sha256','output',
                    'evaluation_envelope_record','evaluation_envelope_sha256'
                )
            }
            expected_exit=[long]0
            expected_terminal_contract=[ordered]@{
                schema_version='complete-suite-selection-terminal-contract-v1'
                classification='families-plus-exact-nodes'
                ordered_families=$task10Families
                ordered_exact_nodes=$securityNodes
                family_terminal='passed'
                exact_node_terminal='passed'
                minimum_nodes_per_family=[long]1
                reject_unclassified_nodes=$true
                forbidden_terminal_states=$forbiddenTerminal
            }
        }
    )
    if ((ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $postRegistry.parsed `
            -Compress -Depth 30) -cne
        (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $expectedSelections `
            -Compress -Depth 30)) {
        throw 'post-trust selection registry semantics mismatch'
    }
    $attributeKeys=@(
        'constructor_class','subject_kinds',
        'permitted_implementation_contexts','proc_thread_attribute_tokens',
        'direct_child_authority'
    )
    foreach ($record in @($attributeRegistry.parsed)) {
        Assert-C6PlanOwnedKeys -Value $record -Expected $attributeKeys `
            -Label 'constructor attribute registry record'
    }
    $topologyKeys=@(
        'topology_id','implicit_campaign_job_kinds',
        'explicit_job_list_kinds','effective_campaign_job_kinds',
        'immediate_scope','completion_owner','termination_owner'
    )
    foreach ($record in @($topologyRegistry.parsed)) {
        Assert-C6PlanOwnedKeys -Value $record -Expected $topologyKeys `
            -Label 'Job topology registry record'
    }
    $rootImplementationContext=[object[]]@(
        'host-native-core-v1','root-broker'
    )
    $standaloneImplementationContext=[object[]]@(
        'host-native-core-v1','standalone-native-leaf'
    )
    $brokerImplementationContext=[object[]]@(
        'broker-native-core-v1','guarded-target-or-native-leaf'
    )
    $clientImplementationContext=[object[]]@(
        'broker-native-core-v1','codex-client-root'
    )
    $expectedAttributes=[object[]]@(
        [ordered]@{
            constructor_class='root-broker'
            subject_kinds=[object[]]@('root-broker')
            permitted_implementation_contexts=(,$rootImplementationContext)
            proc_thread_attribute_tokens=[object[]]@(
                'HANDLE_LIST','JOB_LIST'
            )
            direct_child_authority='closed-broker-api-only'
        },
        [ordered]@{
            constructor_class='guarded-target-or-native-leaf'
            subject_kinds=[object[]]@(
                'guarded-python-target','native-leaf'
            )
            permitted_implementation_contexts=[object[]]@(
                $standaloneImplementationContext,
                $brokerImplementationContext
            )
            proc_thread_attribute_tokens=[object[]]@(
                'HANDLE_LIST','JOB_LIST',
                'CHILD_PROCESS_POLICY=PROCESS_CREATION_CHILD_PROCESS_RESTRICTED'
            )
            direct_child_authority='none'
        },
        [ordered]@{
            constructor_class='codex-client-root'
            subject_kinds=[object[]]@(
                'loopback-codex-client-root','approved-codex-client-root'
            )
            permitted_implementation_contexts=(,$clientImplementationContext)
            proc_thread_attribute_tokens=[object[]]@(
                'HANDLE_LIST','JOB_LIST'
            )
            direct_child_authority=(
                'unchanged-client-declared-descendants-only'
            )
        }
    )
    $expectedTopologies=[object[]]@(
        [ordered]@{
            topology_id='root-broker'
            implicit_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@()
            explicit_job_list_kinds=[object[]]@('J0')
            effective_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@('J0')
            immediate_scope='J0'
            completion_owner='host:P0:J0'
            termination_owner='host:J0'
        },
        [ordered]@{
            topology_id='standalone-native-leaf'
            implicit_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@()
            explicit_job_list_kinds=[object[]]@('L0')
            effective_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@('L0')
            immediate_scope='L0'
            completion_owner='host:P0:L0'
            termination_owner='host:L0'
        },
        [ordered]@{
            topology_id='initial-guarded-target'
            implicit_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@('J0')
            explicit_job_list_kinds=[object[]]@('J1','T0')
            effective_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@('J0','J1','T0')
            immediate_scope='T0'
            completion_owner='root:P1:J1'
            termination_owner='root:T0'
        },
        [ordered]@{
            topology_id='nested-guarded-target'
            implicit_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@('J0')
            explicit_job_list_kinds=[object[]]@('J1','T0..Tk','Tnew')
            effective_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@(
                'J0','J1','T0..Tk','Tnew'
            )
            immediate_scope='Tnew'
            completion_owner='root:P1:J1'
            termination_owner='root:Tnew'
        },
        [ordered]@{
            topology_id='broker-native-leaf'
            implicit_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@('J0')
            explicit_job_list_kinds=[object[]]@('J1','T0..Tk','Ln')
            effective_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@(
                'J0','J1','T0..Tk','Ln'
            )
            immediate_scope='Ln'
            completion_owner='root:P1:J1'
            termination_owner='root:Ln'
        },
        [ordered]@{
            topology_id='codex-client-root'
            implicit_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@('J0')
            explicit_job_list_kinds=[object[]]@('J1','T0..Tk','Cn')
            effective_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@(
                'J0','J1','T0..Tk','Cn'
            )
            immediate_scope='Cn'
            completion_owner='root:P1:J1'
            termination_owner='root:Cn'
        },
        [ordered]@{
            topology_id='codex-client-descendant'
            implicit_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@(
                'parent-effective-chain'
            )
            explicit_job_list_kinds=[object[]]@()
            effective_campaign_job_kinds=[object[]]@(
                'parent-effective-chain'
            )
            immediate_scope='inherited-Cn'
            completion_owner='root:P1:J1'
            termination_owner='root:Cn'
        }
    )
    if ((ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $attributeRegistry.parsed `
            -Compress -Depth 30) -cne
            (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $expectedAttributes `
                -Compress -Depth 30) -or
        (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $topologyRegistry.parsed `
            -Compress -Depth 30) -cne
            (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $expectedTopologies `
                -Compress -Depth 30)) {
        throw 'constructor attribute or Job topology semantics mismatch'
    }
    $hostBodySha=Get-C6PlanOwnedImplementationBodySha256 -Text $controlText `
        -BeginLine '# C6-HOST-NATIVE-CONSTRUCTOR-IMPLEMENTATION-BEGIN' `
        -EndLine '# C6-HOST-NATIVE-CONSTRUCTOR-IMPLEMENTATION-END'
    $brokerBodySha=Get-C6PlanOwnedImplementationBodySha256 -Text $bootstrapText `
        -BeginLine '# C6-BROKER-NATIVE-CONSTRUCTOR-IMPLEMENTATION-BEGIN' `
        -EndLine '# C6-BROKER-NATIVE-CONSTRUCTOR-IMPLEMENTATION-END'
    $implementationRecords=@($implementationRegistry.parsed)
    $implementationKeys=@(
        'constructor_implementation_id','source_relative_path',
        'implementation_sha256','permitted_contexts'
    )
    Assert-C6PlanOwnedKeys -Value $implementationRecords[0] `
        -Expected $implementationKeys -Label 'host constructor registry record'
    Assert-C6PlanOwnedKeys -Value $implementationRecords[1] `
        -Expected $implementationKeys -Label 'broker constructor registry record'
    if ($implementationRecords[0].source_relative_path -cne $controlRelative -or
        $implementationRecords[0].implementation_sha256 -cne $hostBodySha -or
        (@($implementationRecords[0].permitted_contexts) -join "`n") -cne
            "root-broker`nstandalone-native-leaf" -or
        $implementationRecords[1].source_relative_path -cne $bootstrapRelative -or
        $implementationRecords[1].implementation_sha256 -cne $brokerBodySha -or
        (@($implementationRecords[1].permitted_contexts) -join "`n") -cne
            "guarded-target-or-native-leaf`ncodex-client-root") {
        throw 'constructor implementation registry/body mismatch'
    }

    $finalSourceHead=ConvertFrom-C6Task9SingleLine `
        -Bytes (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role source-head @gitArgs) `
        -Label final-source-head -Pattern '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'
    $finalSourceTree=ConvertFrom-C6Task9SingleLine `
        -Bytes (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role source-tree @gitArgs) `
        -Label final-source-tree -Pattern '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'
    $finalCheckoutHead=ConvertFrom-C6Task9SingleLine `
        -Bytes (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role checkout-head @gitArgs) `
        -Label final-checkout-head -Pattern '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'
    $finalCheckoutTree=ConvertFrom-C6Task9SingleLine `
        -Bytes (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role checkout-tree @gitArgs) `
        -Label final-checkout-tree -Pattern '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'
    $finalOracleHead=ConvertFrom-C6Task9SingleLine `
        -Bytes (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role oracle-head @gitArgs) `
        -Label final-oracle-head -Pattern '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'
    $finalOracleTree=ConvertFrom-C6Task9SingleLine `
        -Bytes (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role oracle-tree @gitArgs) `
        -Label final-oracle-tree -Pattern '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'
    if ($finalSourceHead -cne $ExpectedTask9Commit -or
        $finalSourceTree -cne $sourceTree -or
        $finalCheckoutHead -cne $ExpectedTask9Commit -or
        $finalCheckoutTree -cne $sourceTree -or
        $finalOracleHead -cne $artifactOracleHandoff.artifact_oracle_commit -or
        $finalOracleTree -cne $artifactOracleHandoff.artifact_oracle_tree -or
        (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role source-status @gitArgs).Length -ne 0 -or
        (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role checkout-status @gitArgs).Length -ne 0 -or
        (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role checkout-detached @gitArgs).Length -ne 0 -or
        (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role oracle-status @gitArgs).Length -ne 0 -or
        (Invoke-C6Task9PostcheckGit -Role oracle-detached @gitArgs).Length -ne 0) {
        throw 'Task 9 source/checkout/oracle changed during the closed postcheck'
    }

    $zeroRoot='D:\tmp\kokoroarc-c6-zero-codex-envelope-' +
        [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N')
    $transitionRoot='D:\tmp\kokoroarc-c6-task09-transition-' +
        [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N')
    if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $zeroRoot) -or
        (Test-Path -LiteralPath $transitionRoot)) {
        throw 'Task 9 generated output root unexpectedly exists'
    }
    return [ordered]@{
        plan_commit=[string]$handoff.plan.commit
        plan_tree=[string]$handoff.plan.tree
        plan_blob=[string]$handoff.plan.blob
        plan_sha256=[string]$handoff.plan.sha256
        handoff_path=$HandoffPath
        handoff_sha256=$ExpectedHandoffSha256
        task8_commit=$ExpectedTask8Commit
        task9_commit=$ExpectedTask9Commit
        task9_tree=$sourceTree
        post_trust_selection_registry_sha256=$postRegistry.sha256
        host_constructor_implementation_sha256=$hostBodySha
        broker_constructor_implementation_sha256=$brokerBodySha
        constructor_implementation_set_sha256=$implementationRegistry.sha256
        constructor_attribute_set_sha256=$attributeRegistry.sha256
        job_topology_sha256=$topologyRegistry.sha256
        artifact_tty_contract_sha256=$artifactTtyContract.sha256
        artifact_oracle_path=$expectedOraclePath
        artifact_oracle_commit=[string]$artifactOracleHandoff.artifact_oracle_commit
        artifact_oracle_tree=[string]$artifactOracleHandoff.artifact_oracle_tree
        artifact_oracle_blob=[string]$artifactOracleHandoff.artifact_oracle_blob
        artifact_oracle_size=[long]$artifactOracleHandoff.artifact_oracle_size
        artifact_oracle_sha256=[string]$artifactOracleHandoff.artifact_oracle_sha256
        artifact_oracle_review_result_sha256=(
            [string]$artifactOracleHandoff.review_result_sha256
        )
        artifact_oracle_digest_count=[long]8
        checkout_root=$CheckoutRoot
        checkout_entries=[object[]]$entries.ToArray()
        zero_envelope_root=$zeroRoot
        transition_root=$transitionRoot
    }
    } finally {
        foreach ($heldRecord in $oracleHeldRecords) {
            try { Confirm-C6PlanOwnedHeldJson -Held $heldRecord } finally {
                $heldRecord.opened.Dispose()
            }
        }
    }
}

function Write-C6Task9TransitionArtifacts {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [Collections.IDictionary]$Task9TransitionInputs
    )
    $inputKeys=@(
        'plan_commit','plan_tree','plan_blob','plan_sha256',
        'handoff_path','handoff_sha256','task8_commit','task9_commit',
        'task9_tree','post_trust_selection_registry_sha256',
        'host_constructor_implementation_sha256',
        'broker_constructor_implementation_sha256',
        'constructor_implementation_set_sha256',
        'constructor_attribute_set_sha256','job_topology_sha256',
        'artifact_tty_contract_sha256',
        'artifact_oracle_path','artifact_oracle_commit','artifact_oracle_tree',
        'artifact_oracle_blob','artifact_oracle_size','artifact_oracle_sha256',
        'artifact_oracle_review_result_sha256','artifact_oracle_digest_count',
        'checkout_root','checkout_entries',
        'zero_envelope_root','transition_root'
    )
    Assert-C6PlanOwnedKeys -Value $Task9TransitionInputs `
        -Expected $inputKeys -Label 'Task9TransitionInputs'
    foreach ($name in @(
        'plan_commit','plan_tree','plan_blob','task8_commit','task9_commit',
        'task9_tree','artifact_oracle_commit','artifact_oracle_tree',
        'artifact_oracle_blob'
    )) {
        if ($Task9TransitionInputs[$name] -isnot [string] -or
            $Task9TransitionInputs[$name] -cnotmatch '^[0-9a-f]{40}$') {
            throw "invalid 40-hex Task 9 input: $name"
        }
    }
    foreach ($name in @(
        'plan_sha256','handoff_sha256',
        'post_trust_selection_registry_sha256',
        'host_constructor_implementation_sha256',
        'broker_constructor_implementation_sha256',
        'constructor_implementation_set_sha256',
        'constructor_attribute_set_sha256','job_topology_sha256',
        'artifact_tty_contract_sha256','artifact_oracle_sha256',
        'artifact_oracle_review_result_sha256'
    )) {
        if ($Task9TransitionInputs[$name] -isnot [string] -or
            $Task9TransitionInputs[$name] -cnotmatch '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') {
            throw "invalid 64-hex Task 9 input: $name"
        }
    }
    if ($Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_path -isnot [string] -or
        $Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_size -isnot [long] -or
        $Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_size -lt 2 -or
        $Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_size -gt 65536 -or
        $Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_digest_count -isnot [long] -or
        $Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_digest_count -ne 8) {
        throw 'invalid artifact-oracle Task 9 input'
    }
    $checkoutRoot=[string]$Task9TransitionInputs.checkout_root
    $zeroRoot=[string]$Task9TransitionInputs.zero_envelope_root
    $transitionRoot=[string]$Task9TransitionInputs.transition_root
    if ($checkoutRoot -cnotmatch
            '\AD:\\tmp\\kokoroarc-c6-task09-checkout-[0-9a-f]{32}\z' -or
        $zeroRoot -cnotmatch
            '\AD:\\tmp\\kokoroarc-c6-zero-codex-envelope-[0-9a-f]{32}\z' -or
        $transitionRoot -cnotmatch
            '\AD:\\tmp\\kokoroarc-c6-task09-transition-[0-9a-f]{32}\z' -or
        (Test-Path -LiteralPath $zeroRoot) -or
        (Test-Path -LiteralPath $transitionRoot)) {
        throw 'Task 9 roots violate their closed fresh-root grammar'
    }
    $checkoutItem=Get-Item -LiteralPath $checkoutRoot -Force -ErrorAction Stop
    if (-not $checkoutItem.PSIsContainer -or
        (($checkoutItem.Attributes -band [IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) -ne 0)) {
        throw 'Task 9 checkout root is not an observed plain directory'
    }
    [void](Read-C6PlanOwnedJson `
        -Path ([string]$Task9TransitionInputs.handoff_path) `
        -ExpectedSha256 ([string]$Task9TransitionInputs.handoff_sha256) `
        -MaxBytes 65536)
    if ([string]$Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_path -cnotmatch
            '\AD:\\tmp\\kokoroarc-c6-task9-artifact-source-oracle-checkout-' +
            '[0-9a-f]{32}\\docs\\superpowers\\plans\\' +
            '2026-08-21-kokoroarc-complete-suite-campaign-6-' +
            'task9-artifact-source-oracle\.json\z') {
        throw 'artifact-oracle path is outside its authenticated checkout grammar'
    }
    $oracleHeldForWrite=Read-C6PlanOwnedHeldJson `
        -Path ([string]$Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_path) `
        -ExpectedSha256 ([string]$Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_sha256) `
        -MaxBytes 65536 -Role artifact-oracle-write-stage
    try {
    if ($oracleHeldForWrite.bytes.Length -ne
            $Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_size -or
        (Get-C6PlanOwnedGitBlobOid $oracleHeldForWrite.bytes) -cne
            $Task9TransitionInputs.artifact_oracle_blob) {
        throw 'artifact-oracle write-stage tuple mismatch'
    }

    $entryKeys=@(
        'relative_path','mode','blob','size','sha256','lf_only','nul_free'
    )
    $entries=@($Task9TransitionInputs.checkout_entries)
    if ($entries.Count -lt 1 -or $entries.Count -gt 50000) {
        throw 'Task 9 checkout entry count is outside 1..50000'
    }
    [long]$maxCheckoutBytes=1073741824L
    [long]$maxEntryProjectionBytes=7340032L
    [long]$maxManifestBytes=8388608L
    $strictUtf8=[Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false,$true)
    $entryProjectionStream=[IO.MemoryStream]::new()
    $entryProjectionStream.WriteByte(91)
    $normalized=[Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $entryMap=[Collections.Generic.Dictionary[string,object]]::new(
        [StringComparer]::Ordinal
    )
    $caseFolded=[Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new(
        [StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
    )
    $previous=''
    [long]$totalBytes=0
    foreach ($entry in $entries) {
        if ($entry -isnot [Collections.IDictionary]) {
            throw 'Task 9 checkout entry is not an ordered object'
        }
        Assert-C6PlanOwnedKeys -Value $entry -Expected $entryKeys `
            -Label 'Task 9 checkout entry'
        $relative=[string]$entry.relative_path
        $segments=$relative.Split('/')
        if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($relative) -or
            [IO.Path]::IsPathFullyQualified($relative) -or
            $relative.Contains('\') -or $relative.Contains(':') -or
            $relative.Contains([char]0) -or $relative.Contains('//') -or
            $segments -contains '.' -or $segments -contains '..' -or
            ($previous.Length -gt 0 -and
                [StringComparer]::Ordinal.Compare($previous,$relative) -ge 0) -or
            -not $caseFolded.Add($relative)) {
            throw "invalid, duplicate, or unsorted checkout path: $relative"
        }
        if ($entry.mode -isnot [string] -or
            @('100644','100755') -cnotcontains $entry.mode -or
            $entry.blob -isnot [string] -or
            $entry.blob -cnotmatch '^[0-9a-f]{40}$' -or
            $entry.sha256 -isnot [string] -or
            $entry.sha256 -cnotmatch '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' -or
            $entry.size -isnot [long] -or $entry.size -lt 0 -or
            $entry.lf_only -isnot [bool] -or
            $entry.nul_free -isnot [bool]) {
            throw "invalid checkout entry scalar: $relative"
        }
        $absolute=Resolve-C6PlanOwnedPlainFile -Root $checkoutRoot `
            -RelativePath $relative
        if ([IO.Path]::GetRelativePath($checkoutRoot,$absolute).Replace(
                [char]92,[char]47
            ) -cne $relative) {
            throw "checkout entry escapes or aliases its root: $relative"
        }
        if ($totalBytes -gt $maxCheckoutBytes - $entry.size) {
            throw 'Task 9 checkout aggregate exceeds 1 GiB'
        }
        $totalBytes += $entry.size
        $shaHasher=[Security.Cryptography.IncrementalHash]::CreateHash(
            [Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName]::SHA256
        )
        $blobHasher=[Security.Cryptography.IncrementalHash]::CreateHash(
            [Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName]::SHA1
        )
        $opened=$null
        $memberFailure=$null
        try {
            $opened=[C6PlanOwnedNativeFile]::OpenRegular($absolute)
            if ($opened.Length -gt 268435456 -or
                $opened.Length -ne $entry.size) {
                throw "checkout member type/size mismatch: $relative"
            }
            $memberIdentity=$opened.Identity
            $memberLength=$opened.Length
            $header=[Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes(
                'blob ' + $entry.size + [char]0
            )
            $blobHasher.AppendData($header)
            [byte[]]$buffer=[byte[]]::new(65536)
            [long]$fileBytesRead=0
            $hasCr=$false
            $hasNul=$false
            while (($count=$opened.Stream.Read(
                        $buffer,0,$buffer.Length
                    )) -gt 0) {
                if ($fileBytesRead + $count -gt $entry.size) {
                    throw "checkout member grew while hashing: $relative"
                }
                $shaHasher.AppendData($buffer,0,$count)
                $blobHasher.AppendData($buffer,0,$count)
                for ($byteIndex=0; $byteIndex -lt $count; $byteIndex++) {
                    if ($buffer[$byteIndex] -eq 13) { $hasCr=$true }
                    if ($buffer[$byteIndex] -eq 0) { $hasNul=$true }
                }
                $fileBytesRead += $count
            }
            $actualSha256=[Convert]::ToHexString(
                $shaHasher.GetHashAndReset()
            ).ToLowerInvariant()
            $actualBlob=[Convert]::ToHexString(
                $blobHasher.GetHashAndReset()
            ).ToLowerInvariant()
        } catch {
            $memberFailure=$_
            throw
        } finally {
            $cleanupFailure=$null
            foreach ($cleanup in @(
                [pscustomobject]@{
                    value=$opened
                    key='C6FinalCheckoutNativeHandleDisposeFailure'
                },
                [pscustomobject]@{
                    value=$shaHasher
                    key='C6FinalCheckoutSha256DisposeFailure'
                },
                [pscustomobject]@{
                    value=$blobHasher
                    key='C6FinalCheckoutBlobDisposeFailure'
                }
            )) {
                if ($null -ne $cleanup.value) {
                    try {
                        $cleanup.value.Dispose()
                    } catch {
                        if ($null -ne $memberFailure) {
                            $memberFailure.Exception.Data[$cleanup.key]=(
                                $_.Exception.Message
                            )
                        } elseif ($null -eq $cleanupFailure) {
                            $cleanupFailure=$_
                        } else {
                            $cleanupFailure.Exception.Data[$cleanup.key]=(
                                $_.Exception.Message
                            )
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            if ($null -eq $memberFailure -and $null -ne $cleanupFailure) {
                throw $cleanupFailure
            }
        }
        $post=$null
        $postFailure=$null
        try {
            $post=[C6PlanOwnedNativeFile]::OpenRegular($absolute)
            if ($post.Identity -cne $memberIdentity -or
                $post.Length -ne $memberLength -or
                $post.Length -ne $entry.size) {
                throw "checkout member identity drift: $relative"
            }
        } catch {
            $postFailure=$_
            throw
        } finally {
            if ($null -ne $post) {
                try {
                    $post.Dispose()
                } catch {
                    if ($null -ne $postFailure) {
                        $postFailure.Exception.Data[
                            'C6FinalCheckoutPostHandleDisposeFailure'
                        ]=$_.Exception.Message
                    } else {
                        throw
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        [void](Resolve-C6PlanOwnedPlainFile -Root $checkoutRoot `
            -RelativePath $relative)
        if ($fileBytesRead -ne $entry.size -or
            $actualSha256 -cne $entry.sha256 -or
            $entry.lf_only -ne (-not $hasCr) -or
            $entry.nul_free -ne (-not $hasNul)) {
            throw "checkout member byte projection mismatch: $relative"
        }
        if ($actualBlob -cne $entry.blob) {
            throw "checkout member Git blob mismatch: $relative"
        }
        $normalizedEntry=[ordered]@{
            relative_path=$relative
            mode=[string]$entry.mode
~~~

Compute `R = SHA256(receipt bytes)` only after the receipt closes and pass its
literal value outside the receipt in the successor argv. This local four-record
DAG extends, and does not replace, the already authenticated `H`/`O` chain:
`M` has no local terminal dependency, trust record `T` names `M` plus `H`/`O`,
`X` names `T`, `M`, and the same oracle hashes, and `R` names all three plus the
same eight oracle-chain fields. Terminal-record creation is not appended to an
invented operation chain. No repository/test code writes these records.

An index byte change, a failed commit/postcheck, or any later trust-file change
invalidates the attempt. Retain it untouched and restart Task 9 from the exact
Task 8 commit in a fresh branch/worktree/root; never amend, reset, or let failed
Task 9 bytes become their own attestation.

- [ ] **Step 10: Run the four installed-client renderer conformance probes from committed bytes**

Invoke the exact installed native `codex.exe` four times with `codex exec`, the
same campaign shell-environment overrides, exact evaluator model,
`--ignore-rules`, no inherited project or user config, web search disabled,
MCP/apps/hooks absent, and only the case-local loopback provider above. This is
an installed-client renderer/tool conformance proof, not a provider/model run.
It may connect only to the owned loopback socket. The first two invocations run
the inert `Test-Path`; parse each JSONL command event, recover the actual
rendered process-argument bytes, and pass them through
`extract_powershell_payload`. Freeze the exact command `item.started`/
`item.completed` schema and prove completion exposes one `aggregated_output`
string plus one command-record integer exit code and no per-command
stdout/stderr fields. Require the frozen shell path, all four flags, exact
payload, matching event ID/bytes, exit zero, expected merged inert output, empty
Codex-process stderr, and identical repeated normalized events.

The third invocation performs only the closed add and the fourth performs only
the closed update. Write their complete client JSONL bytes to two distinct new
no-follow capture files and retain each path, identity, UTF-8 size, and SHA-256;
never create a combined stream. Freeze the exact outer JSONL shapes
`{"type":"item.started","item":...}` and
`{"type":"item.completed","item":...}`. The item is recursively closed to
exactly `id`, `type:"file_change"`, `changes`, and `status`; started status is
`in_progress`, completed status is `completed`, and both records require the
same exact unnormalized ID and ordered one-item `changes` array. Each change is
recursively closed to the exact raw absolute audit-root `path` and literal
`kind:add|update`. Bind that raw path separately from its normalized relative
path, which must be exactly `preflight-file-change.txt`; neither representation
may substitute for the other. Require absence of shell-command events. Hash the

preloaded-type coverage without attempting to compile or reuse a type in the
writer boundary. The test never tries to change FullLanguage, ConstrainedLanguage,
sandbox, or another security policy.

the retained authenticated ScriptBlock and that PSModulePath is
absent from the inner environment. Static PowerShell AST and transcript checks
reject Import-Module, Get-Module, Add-Type, Get-ChildItem, Sort-Object, any
module-qualified variant, or any other command invocation in the artifact
launcher. Because the inner is Python, there is no accepted PowerShell module
path/hash/source identity at this boundary: a mutant that adds one rejects before
artifact mutation rather than authenticating or loading it.

`guarded-pytest-audit` is the sole operator-facing pytest entry point after its
Task 10 implementation. Each literal `selection` maps inside reviewed code to
one exact file/node/filter/cwd/environment contract; arbitrary pytest argv,
plugins, paths, shell text, or environment overlays are not accepted. It runs
two fresh guarded collections and one fresh guarded execution through the same
`_release-pytest-capture` broker used by `release-gate-audit`, requires the
ordered node sets to match, and publishes one canonical
`complete-suite-guarded-pytest-audit-v1` record only after every selected node
has its closed expected terminal outcome. The mutation-coverage selection runs
its expected failing inner mutants beneath broker-owned disposable checkouts;
the outer selected nodes must pass and bind every killed predicate.

Freeze the selection map in the committed Task 9 control-plane trust anchor
rather than constructing it from caller text or Task 10 staged bytes. The first
four entries form this exact ordered post-trust selection registry. Each tuple
ends with the literal suffix `-q`, `-p`, `no:cacheprovider`, `--basetemp`, and
the closed `BROKER_BASETEMP` path token. For `development-pytest` that token is
the broker-created absent `phase_root`; for `guarded-pytest-audit` it is the
operation/ordinal-specific absent child derived internally beneath that root.
Neither a caller nor staged Task 10 code may add, remove, reorder, or derive a
token. Each record has exactly these ordered keys: `selection`, `adapter`,
`pytest_argv`, `binding_keys`, `expected_exit`, and
`expected_terminal_contract`. The first three records' `binding_keys` value is
an ordered string array. `task10-integrated` instead has an ordered object with
exact keys `authenticated-provisional`, `commit`; each value is the exact
ordered string array below. No mode may accept the other mode's array.

Every `expected_terminal_contract` is an ordered object with exact keys
`schema_version`, `classification`, `ordered_families`,
`ordered_exact_nodes`, `family_terminal`, `exact_node_terminal`,
`minimum_nodes_per_family`, `reject_unclassified_nodes`, and
`forbidden_terminal_states`. Its schema is
`complete-suite-selection-terminal-contract-v1`; its forbidden-state array is
always exactly `skipped`, `xfailed`, `xpassed`, `rerun`, `missing`, `error`.
`classification` is exactly `families`, `exact-nodes`, or
`families-plus-exact-nodes`; unused terminal fields are JSON null and unused
arrays are empty. The family/node arrays and expected terminals are the literal
values stated for each entry below, the minimum is one for every family-bearing
entry and zero otherwise, and `reject_unclassified_nodes` is always true.
The last value is therefore the canonical compact projection of the node/
failure rules stated for that entry below.
The registry serializes those values to canonical bytes. Its
`post_trust_selection_registry_sha256` is bound into the Task 9 transition,
trust-anchor record, every later control-plane receipt, and every selected root/
target descriptor. A missing/extra key or registry digest mismatch rejects
before collection or execution.

`task15-retained-replay`, `task15-adjudication-replay`. It runs each selection

The Task 9 trust-anchor REDs assert byte-for-byte canonical equality for all

and the execution. Every argv/filter mutation rejects before execution or
record publication. Task 11 invokes only the two already named historical/
mutation families; it never adds or changes a selection. A selection-map byte
change after the Task 9 trust commit invalidates the trust anchor and returns to
Task 9, never merely to a later RED review.

`guard-source=client-preflight` is permitted only for `task10-integrated` and
the four Task 11 selections. It requires both guard-record arguments, forbids

selections. It requires the campaign plus expected hash, forbids guard-
record arguments, and derives the same guard authority only from the campaign-
bound candidate-input aggregate; no caller may override a descendant path or
identity. Both modes recapture their authority before and after every child.
They derive every Python target and overlay from that authority and the closed
selection/phase map; neither mode accepts a runtime, package, import-root, or
target-role override.

`source-identity-mode=authenticated-provisional` is permitted only for the Task
10 integrated audit and the three executed Task 11 selections, requires both
provisional-record fields, and forbids `expected-head` and both prior-audit
fields; its source root must be the authenticated detached materialization of
that exact parent/tree/record. Commit mode forbids provisional fields and
requires exact HEAD/tree/parent. The prior-audit pair is all-or-none, is required
only for commit-mode `task10-integrated`, and is forbidden for every other
selection/mode. It must authenticate the exact same-selection
`authenticated-provisional` record with equal authority, parent, tree,

terminal outcomes, and stable skip projection; the new committed audit must
match that stable projection byte-for-byte.
Uncommitted-primary-approved6 mode is permitted only for the two Task 15

`expected_prior_audit_record_sha256`. Unknown, missing, reordered, partial, or

The phase root and sibling output must both be absent, GUID-qualified, and
created no-replace; neither may be beneath the repository, a campaign root, or

ordered broker descendant/target-role tree, guarded-runtime and overlay
manifest hashes, and literal `codex_attempts:0`. Every root or

`sealed-campaign-audit` is read-only with respect to the repository, raw root,
reservation directory, and retained root. It captures and revalidates no-follow
identities/membership before and after inspection. Its closed result class is
exactly one of `sealed_24_run`, `sealed_zero_run_failure`,
`reserved_zero_run_failure`, or `invalid_consumed_attempt`. The normal class
replays the provider approval, authorization-consumption reservation, execute-
consumption marker, claim, completion,
inventory, seal, `COMPLETED`, all 24 unique ledgers, capture/artifact/final-event
hashes and counts, all 24 run-intent/evaluation-envelope/launch-spec/template
records and their ordered launch-evidence manifest, and requires the retained
root absent. It also reopens the canonical persisted credential-pipe/lifecycle
pair and requires its hashes and reference to equal the non-null
`credential-accepted` projections in the completion, inventory, and seal; the
live host/root/target terminal agreement was already a mandatory condition of
the completed `execute` transition. Zero-run classes bind
the exact reservation, optional execute-consumption marker, terminal, or raw-
root zero-run seal with 0 starts and no 24-ledger requirement; reserved branches
require both terminal lifecycle fields null, while claimed-root branches require
the exact null-or-hash-pair projection dictated by the readiness boundary. The
invalid class
records only bounded reference hashes and before/after no-follow facts and
performs no repair. An exact execute-consumption marker with no raw root and no
canonical terminal is a consumed, unsealed `invalid_consumed_attempt`, never
permission to execute again. It emits one canonical
out-of-tree `complete-suite-sealed-campaign-audit-v1` record; only
`sealed_24_run` may be used to request import authorization.
It exits zero after safely publishing any one of the four closed classes so the
caller can branch mechanically. An invalid CLI/precondition or inspection state
too indeterminate to classify exits nonzero and publishes no output. RED tests
cover all four zero-exit records and the nonzero/no-output cases while asserting
zero credential/environment read, descendant-process/socket/network call, or raw/retained/
repository write.

`pre-freeze-gate-audit` is the sole Task 12 mechanical gate. It runs only the
approved design Section 10 pre-freeze work: the complete focused Campaign 6
harness, the named researching-character command-safety regressions, immutable
Approved1-through-Approved5 legacy replay, mutation coverage, compile and
whitespace checks, the sensitive-material scan, and one fresh local
`core.autocrlf=true` checkout. The primary checkout and fresh checkout must
agree on approval-bound bytes, parser identity, plan hash, selected ordered node
IDs, terminal outcomes, and stable skip codes. It performs no complete test
collection, build, installed wheel/sdist workflow, Skill/plugin validation,

`complete-suite-pre-freeze-gate-v1`; immediately after that immutable sibling
output it exclusively publishes the phase-root `host-review-input-bundle.json`
for the exact candidate target. The later review envelope independently binds
both, avoiding a self-hash cycle. REDs fail immediately before/after record and
bundle CreateNew: a record-only or partial bundle attempt is retained but cannot
be reviewed. Its evidence-entry subsequence is exactly the two candidate table
rows (`00` pre-freeze-gate, then `01` candidate-input-aggregate), both at mode
`100644`; omission/substitution/order/ordinal/role/leaf/mode/cap drift publishes
no review input. Repeated production from identical fixed inputs in a separate
process must produce the same canonical bundle bytes and SHA-256.
Every pytest child is zero-Codex, while the
four separately enveloped Task 12 loopback Codex probes remain constituents of
the already-frozen candidate-input aggregate rather than children of this gate.

`release-gate-audit` is the sole mechanical producer for post-closure release
records. In `closure-committed` and `final-docs` it exclusively publishes the
phase-root `host-review-input-bundle.json` after the immutable sibling release
record so that record is an exact bundle entry; the later review envelope
independently binds both and the other two phases forbid that leaf. The
`closure-committed` evidence subsequence is exactly its seven table rows: its
own release plus the candidate specification and quality/security PASS
envelope/result/audit triplets. The `final-docs` evidence subsequence is exactly
its nine table rows: its three high-level subjects plus the closure
specification and quality/security PASS envelope/result/audit triplets. Every
one of those out-of-tree rows has mode `100644`, and each source is selected by
the table binding rather than a caller argument or directory search. Its reviewed subprocess adapter always captures a
bounded argv/environment/result, checks a native return code before the next
operation, and rejects provider/network/credential access. It accepts no
caller-selected wheelhouse, validator, or preflight path: it reopens only the
aggregate-record path/hash stored in `campaign.frozen_inputs.candidate_inputs`,
requires that record and every derived child to match before and after each
subprocess family, including the complete guarded-Python runtime and every
role-specific overlay, and binds the aggregate record/hash into its output. For
each of the closed `focused`, `unit`, `integration`, `security`, and `skills`
selection IDs inside each of the independently materialized A and B checkouts,
it performs two independent collections and two independent executions in
fresh child processes. Every `(phase, checkout-role, selection, operation,
ordinal)` receives a distinct broker-owned basetemp. The producer retains all
ten checkout-selection records, stores ordered node IDs and stable outcome/
skip-code digests, requires the two collections and two executions within each
record to agree, and requires the comparable A/B projection to agree for all
five selections before it emits their stable comparison projection. It performs
compile audit, two isolated local autocrlf materializations, A/B builds, exact wheel
byte/hash equality, normalized sdist inventory equality, installed wheel/sdist
workflow node/outcome equality, frozen-validator audits, LF/diff/status/legacy
inventory checks, and the phase-specific approved6 rule. Every pytest child is
a strict zero-Codex zone; no evaluation envelope authorizes an exception. The
producer separately revalidates and binds the Task 12 aggregate's truthful
loopback-envelope manifest and, after execution, the 24 real launch-evidence
records. Missing/overbroad/mismatched metadata still fails and never relaxes
sandbox, network, or security policy. The output is one canonical
`complete-suite-release-gate-audit-v1` record with every collection, outcome,
artifact, validator, checkout, guarded-runtime/target/overlay, and evaluation-
envelope digest. The `closure-precommit` invocation requires and binds the exact
Task 12 pre-freeze-gate record/hash, but that record is not treated as a prior
release record; later phases bind the immediately preceding post-closure release
record. A `candidate` phase or `approved6-mode=absent` rejects at argument
validation before a child starts.

That full five-selection/build/validator matrix executes only in
`closure-precommit` and `closure-committed`. The later `closure-reviewed` and
`final-docs` modes reopen and revalidate all immutable artifact/validator/matrix
bindings from their predecessor but execute only the exact two approved6 replay
selections and their phase-specific primary/A/B projections described below.
They cannot substitute a reduced run for either earlier full gate.

The runner's private `_release-pytest-capture` child uses `pytest.main` plus a
reviewed hook to emit one bounded canonical record containing every collected
node ID and terminal outcome. It rejects duplicate node IDs, collection errors,
xfail/xpass/rerun, unknown skip codes, missing terminals, stdout protocol noise,
and every Codex launch attempt. Before importing pytest, plugins, repository
modules, or tests, the parent verifies a canonical guard record against the
campaign-bound aggregate's no-follow Codex path/identity/hash and installs one
reviewed in-process broker. The committed host first creates the trusted
`root-broker` with the root constructor class and therefore without the child-
process restriction. That broker imports no pytest or repository role; after
its own ACK/GO it creates the initial child-process-restricted
`root_role_entrypoint` target, and only that target imports the capture role.
The root-broker then owns the only OS process-creation callback for the complete
pytest descendant tree. Every guarded target and every brokered native leaf,
but not the trusted root-broker or the separately classified Codex client TCB,
has verified Windows child-process-restricted mitigation and therefore no OS
right to create another process. The broker resolves every requested executable
no-follow and rejects the frozen Codex identity, name, `PATH` alias, hardlink,
shell-transitive form, unknown executable, `shell=True`, or changed argv/input
contract before creation.

For every guarded Python target, including the target whose logical role is
`root_role_entrypoint`, the broker derives and revalidates
`FrozenGuardedPythonRuntime` solely from that guard authority. It never consults
current `site`, a caller runtime path, or package discovery. The only permitted
guarded-target Python OS argv is exactly
`<frozen-runtime-python> -I -S -B -c <the fixed loader source above> --
--bootstrap-path <authenticated frozen bootstrap> --bootstrap-sha256 <bound
bootstrap hash> --descriptor-handle <single-use-handle> --ack-handle
<single-use-handle> --go-handle <single-use-handle>`. The guarded-target
bootstrap validates the single-use descriptor/ACK/GO channels,
Python/bootstrap/runtime identities and hashes, `_pth` facts, and active OS
child restriction before importing target code. It installs the audit/process/import guards, validates all
already loaded modules as builtin, frozen, or frozen-stdlib members, sets
`sys.dont_write_bytecode=True`, clears importer caches, disables pytest plugin
autoload, and replaces `sys.path` exactly with: the descriptor's captured
target overlays in closed role order; frozen `runtime-site` (except that
`validator_audit` substitutes the separately frozen validator runtime and may
not see general `runtime-site`); optional frozen
stdlib ZIP; frozen `DLLs`; and frozen `Lib`. CWD, repository root by default,
user/system site, environment `PYTHONPATH`, `.pth`, an unknown namespace
constituent, and every origin outside those manifests reject. DLL search is
restricted to the frozen Python/core/DLL/runtime directories plus required
Windows system DLLs, and native-extension identity/hash is recaptured
immediately before and after load.

This paragraph does not describe the trusted root-broker. The host constructs
that process under the `root-broker` constructor row; its authenticated broker
bootstrap validates the root descriptor/ACK/GO handles, query-only outer Job
handle, and absence of child-process restriction, imports only the broker
module, and never imports pytest or repository role code.

`GuardedPythonTarget` is produced only by the broker from a closed logical
request, never decoded from arbitrary generic `-m`, script, or `-c` text. The
only roles are `root_role_entrypoint`, `pytest_capture`, `compile_audit`, `build_frontend`,
`build_backend_hook`, `pip_install`, `source_cli`, `installed_cli`,
`installed_probe`, `approval_bound_test_probe`, `multiprocessing_worker`, and
`validator_audit`. Each role has one reviewed argv/environment/cwd grammar and
exact overlay-role sequence. `root_entrypoint_role` is non-null if and only if
`role="root_role_entrypoint"`; it must equal the enclosing authenticated
`Invoke-C6RootPython` role from the exact 17-value enum, and the target's logical
argv/import entrypoint is derived only from that role's registry row. Every
other target requires null. A target may contain at most eight phase-owned
overlays, 16,384 entries and 1 GiB aggregate; one descriptor is capped at 256
KiB, argv and environment at 64 KiB each, loaded origins at 4,096, descendant
depth at 16, and brokered descendants at 256 per capture. The broker captures
each overlay through bounded no-follow directory-inclusive inventory before
issuing a descriptor and recaptures it after completion. It separately captures
at most eight non-import input/output roots under the same entry/byte caps;
those roots may supply cwd, project source, artifacts, or output targets but are
never inserted into `sys.path`. Descriptor path text is broker-produced under
the source checkout or exclusive phase root and is bound to the role/identity/
manifest; no caller path can override the static runtime. The canonical bounded
descriptor payload carries the actual closed role, actual ordered logical argv,
argv SHA-256, cwd broker token plus exact absolute path and SHA-256, actual
sorted from-scratch environment name/value pairs and SHA-256, runtime and
parent-descriptor hashes, depth/ordinal, the exact ordered
`GuardedInheritedHandle` child-value/role/type/access manifest, and each
overlay/input's broker token/path, root identity, count/bytes, and manifest
hash. It never carries caller
source text, a generic module/script/command, inherited environment, or an
unbound path. The parent retains the full entry arrays. The bootstrap rejects
duplicate keys, an unknown/additional field, noncanonical UTF-8/LF JSON, a
hash/value mismatch, over-limit content, or a value that does not match the
role grammar. It independently recaptures each overlay and recomputes that
manifest before importing it, and rechecks non-import inputs around the target,
so the descriptor cap never truncates authority.

The broker frames the descriptor channel as one four-byte unsigned little-
endian payload length, canonical payload bytes, then EOF. It creates a new
token and the eight fixed-role local named-pipe pairs for every guarded launch,
atomically marks the token `reserved`, and never accepts a numeric handle, pipe
name, or token from target code. The bootstrap reads that exact frame, observes
descriptor EOF, closes `descriptor_read`, validates all bytes and authority,
and emits exactly one authenticated framed `ack` on its dedicated `ack_status`
writer. The broker validates that ACK, writes exactly one authenticated framed
`go` on the dedicated `go` writer, closes it, and the target must observe GO
EOF before it may alter `sys.path` or import target code. `broker_request` and
`broker_response` are not used for either handshake; they remain open after GO
for the bounded sequenced request protocol and close only under its terminal
grammar. Duplicate/read-after-EOF descriptors, missing/duplicate/reordered ACK
or GO frames, a raw GO byte, use of a persistent response pipe for ACK, wrong
PID/creation time, parent-chain mismatch, parent exit before child reservation,
or any handle reuse rejects the entire capture. On every terminal path both
sides follow the common cancellation/close state machine, the parent marks the
token `consumed` exactly once, and no later target can inherit or request it.

Every guarded target uses the class-specific constructor registry above. Its
exact `HANDLE_LIST` is `descriptor_read`, `ack_status`, `go`,
`broker_request`, `broker_response`, `stdin`, `stdout`, `stderr`, plus—only for
the closed multiprocessing role—the descriptor-bound synchronization/queue
objects. Its exact attribute set is `HANDLE_LIST`, the ordered
`[J1,T0,...,Tself]` `JOB_LIST`, and
`CHILD_PROCESS_POLICY=PROCESS_CREATION_CHILD_PROCESS_RESTRICTED`. A native leaf
uses only stdio plus `[J1,T0,...,Tk,Ln]` and the same restriction. A trusted
root uses descriptor/ACK/GO/stdio plus `outer_job_query`, exact `[J0]`, and no
child restriction. A Codex client root uses stdio plus
`[J1,T0,...,Tk,Cn]` and no child restriction. Before creation the applicable
constructor marks every other handle non-inheritable and rejects an unexpected
object type/access mask, duplicate numeric value, pseudo handle, socket, file
outside captured roots, or role-incompatible handle. A guarded bootstrap
recaptures its inherited handle table and proves the active kernel restriction
before ACK; the trusted root bootstrap instead proves the root class, exact
query-only outer Job handle, and absence of that restriction before ACK.
Generic ambient inheritance, an assign-capable outer Job handle, or an unlisted
synchronization primitive is never permitted.

The completion-port ledger monotonically numbers every observed
`JOB_OBJECT_MSG_NEW_PROCESS`, `EXIT_PROCESS`, `ABNORMAL_EXIT_PROCESS`, and
`ACTIVE_PROCESS_ZERO` packet under its typed Job key, but all corresponding
event ordinals are optional because Windows does not guarantee those messages.
After every packet or 50 ms poll timeout the owner queries process handles,
every inner Job's accounting, and each associated Job's accounting plus process
ID list. Each `GuardedProcessRecord` binds PID plus creation time (never PID
alone), OS parent identity, logical parent descriptor, image identity/hash,
implicit/explicit/effective Campaign Job sequences, ordered list digest,
immediate scope, suspended-membership proof, topology digest, I/O completion
owner, termination owner, ambient-ancestor boolean, inherited-handle manifest,
descriptor and constructor hashes, the recomputed native-vector contract/unit
count/UTF-16LE hash, optional event ordinals, process-handle
signal, exit code, and termination state. Each client record binds the
analogous chain, and every client-descendant record repeats the inherited
effective chain. Owners keep all known process handles open until signaled and
`GetExitCodeProcess` reconciles. PID reuse, an unknown process, a process
without a reservation, duplicate or contradictory packet, image/parent/Job-
chain drift, attempted breakaway, broker exception, timeout, orphan, or
unexpected exit terminates the smallest owning Job and prevents success.

Each `JobLifecycleRecord` must finish with `ActiveProcesses == 0`, an empty
process-ID list, and `TotalProcesses` equal to the unique known member count for
that scope. Each noncredential `PipeLifecycleRecord` must finish with its exact
protocol byte count, permitted EOF fact, and zero live I/O. The dedicated
`CredentialPipeLifecycleRecord` must instead finish with exact progress classes,
permitted EOF/error/close facts, and zero live I/O while retaining no payload
length or length-derived digest. Success requires those
authoritative facts, every reserved descriptor consumed once, every known
process handle signaled, and exact bijection among logical launches, kernel
process identities, applicable Job scopes, and terminal results. A missing Job
packet is harmless only if those facts still reconcile; otherwise it fails
closed. `zero descendant` therefore means zero extra OS Job member, not merely
zero logical request.

### Codex-owned client process TCB (normative)

The guarded-process claims above apply only to root Python, Git, Node, the
decoder, and their brokered guarded descendants. They do not apply to an
unchanged Codex client after its root starts. The broker creates the authenticated
native `codex.exe` root suspended and atomically inside its own fresh client Job,
using only the client stdio handle list and intentionally no child-process-
restriction attribute. Codex then creates its own PowerShell/tool descendants.
Those descendants are not claimed to be broker-created, suspended,
descriptor/ACK/GO gated, or prevalidated before their first instruction.

The approval-bound preflight freezes the exact allowed image/parent-role closure
for each loopback or approved-client run, including executable path, identity,
size/hash, permitted parent role, argv/environment policy digest, and the shell/
tool operation limits. The broker combines advisory Job packets with the fixed
50 ms authoritative Job queries. For each newly observed PID it opens the
process with minimum query/synchronize rights, obtains creation time and parent
PID/creation time, resolves and recaptures the full image identity/size/hash,
and correlates it to the command/tool lifecycle before accepting it into a
`ClientDescendantRecord`. PID alone is never authority. An unknown image,
parent, process, or policy mapping immediately terminates `Cn` and invalidates
the run, but the process may already have begun; this is detection/
reconciliation, not a preventative kernel claim. A short-lived process missed
by both notification and polling still increments Job `TotalProcesses`, so the
known-member mismatch fails closed. Success requires the root plus every known
descendant to biject with command/tool records, signaled exit states,
authoritative `Cn` accounting, both output EOFs, and the exact selected client-
limit row in one `ClientProcessRecord`.

The separately approved client TCB is therefore the frozen codex-cli 0.149.0
binary/distribution, its provider/base-URL/TLS behavior, Codex automatic review
and cybersecurity checks, its workspace-write agent-shell sandbox, and the
agent shell's `network_access=false` policy. Evaluation-envelope metadata never
suppresses a security decision, widens the shell sandbox/network policy, or
authorizes an unlisted operation. The Task 13 envelope and exact Task 14 prompt
must disclose and bind both this weaker-but-truthful descendant boundary and the
distinct coarse host network transition before a real provider run can be
approved.

For a pytest target, overlays are only the exact selection-required
`src`, `tests`, `tests\skills`, and/or `tests\integration` roots captured against
the expected Git HEAD/tree/parent; the bare repository root is not an import
root. Disposable mutation checkouts receive new captured overlays. The native-
leaf union is exhaustive: `git`, `node`, and `powershell_decoder`. Each leaf
binds its literal executable path, identity, size/hash/version, exact argv/
environment/cwd grammar hashes, input identities, expected selection count,
and child-process-restricted zero-descendant policy. Inability to apply or
verify that restriction for the initial guarded target or any leaf fails before creation.
Git is reachable only through the single closed Git launcher below. Node has its
one exact manifest-bound argv/environment and must return any requested child
operation to the broker; it may not spawn one. The decoder leaf is the pinned
PowerShell executable with exact `-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File
<captured-decoder>` argv and bounded binary stdin data. `-Command`,
`-EncodedCommand`, another script, or any shell descendant is forbidden. Python
is always a `GuardedPythonTarget`; Codex is the separately approval-bound client/
provider; `fsutil` is unavailable; Git hardlink and junction checks are
broker-owned process-free operations; `rg`, `cmd`, npm, a general shell, and every other
executable reject before OS creation.

Each call supplies its one fixed operation ID and retains the existing product

During a guarded capture the child sends that validated logical request over

The installed-artifact test keeps logical `subprocess.run` calls so its behavior

Each full capture also derives `guarded_target_contract_sha256` from only the

Every leaf must complete with the Windows child-process restriction active,

filter, lazy fetch, maintenance process, or any other logical or OS descendant

inventories, requires HEAD/tree/parent exact, clean status, expected LF/CRLF

argv/environment grammar hashes, fixed checkout semantic assertions, and the

HEAD/tree/parent, source-object identities, phase/root tokens, and complete
admin/index/worktree inventories. Those excluded facts are never ignored: each
full phase record independently binds and validates them against its expected
Git identity and phase-specific allowed-delta manifest. RED mutants prove that
putting any phase identity into the contract digest, or omitting it from the

The four accepted phases have one closed predecessor grammar.
`closure-precommit` requires the exact Task 12 pre-freeze-gate record/hash and

`closure-reviewed` requires both exact specification and quality/security PASS
envelope/result/audit triplets, proves all six artifacts are canonical PASS
bindings for its unchanged closure HEAD/tree/parent and exact prior release
record/equivalence hash, proves both audits authenticate the same exact phase
bundle/projection and the quality audit captures the specification result path/
identity/size/bytes/hash while the specification audit records null, and binds
the two complete triplets
into its successor record. `final-docs` forbids direct review arguments because
their hashes are inherited from its authenticated `closure-reviewed`
predecessor. Each later transition compares the
applicable versioned stable release projection containing sorted node IDs,
terminal outcomes/allowlisted skip codes, exact wheel bytes/hash, normalized
sdist inventory, installed wheel/sdist results, validator results, guarded-
Python runtime manifest and `guarded_target_contract_sha256`, the frozen Git/
Node leaf aggregate and `checkout_materializer_contract_sha256`, LF/legacy
inventories, and the unchanged 28-record preflight evaluation manifest. Full
matrix records are nested first by closed selection ID and then by checkout role
`a|b`. Where a phase runs a selection, its stable comparison projection is emitted only after both
required role records exist and their ordered-node, outcome/skip-code, and
guarded-target-contract projections are equal; no phase may discard or collapse
a role record before proving that equality.
The full per-phase target/overlay/checkout records remain required inputs but
are validated through the phase identity/allowed-delta rules rather than
compared byte-for-byte across different HEADs. `closure-precommit` produces and
internally proves equality for its five A/B matrix projections, validates the
two new primary-worktree approved6 replay projections separately, and performs
only the shared-subset comparison to the Task 12 pre-freeze record described
above. It also adds its exact separately hashed raw/retained/ledger and
24-record real launch-evidence/envelope manifests. Closure-precommit-to-closure-
committed compares the same five A/B matrix projections and requires the
complete approved6 manifest byte-identical; it then requires both committed A
and B records for each of the two approved6 selections to equal each other and
to equal that selection's corresponding closure-precommit primary-worktree
replay projection. `closure-reviewed` runs only the two approved6 replay
selections against the clean primary closure commit and both new A/B
materializations, requires all three projections per selection to match the
corresponding `closure-committed` stable record, and binds both exact PASS review
records without changing the source identity. Final-docs compares only its four A/B records for
`task15-retained-replay` and
`task15-adjudication-replay` to the matching closure-reviewed records, plus
every immutable source/evidence/artifact and prior approved6 field. Every projection excludes durations,
absolute temp paths, raw stdout/stderr, and source HEAD; mismatch publishes no
record.

Node/outcome/target-contract entries are keyed by closed selection ID and keep
their required `a|b` role records until the equality check above succeeds. Each
transition compares exactly its declared common selection keys, never the union:
closure-precommit has no earlier release selection keys and instead validates
its five internal A/B keys, its two primary approved6 replay keys, and the exact
shared pre-freeze subset; closure-precommit-to-closure-committed compares the
same five A/B keys, then validates both committed role records for both
approved6 replay selections against the matching closure-precommit primary
record; closure-committed-to-closure-reviewed compares only the two exact replay
keys across primary/A/B plus the two review bindings; final-docs compares only
the same two exact replay keys,
requires both `a|b` records for each, and requires the predecessor's immutable
approved6/artifact bindings unchanged. A missing, duplicate, swapped,
unexpected, collapsed, or silently
dropped checkout-role or selection key rejects.

`closure-manifest-audit` is the sole closure/cumulative manifest serializer and
comparator. In `worktree` mode it derives the exact sorted path/blob-hash delta
from the filesystem and Git base, checks it against the reviewed closed path/
root allowlist, and writes canonical `closure-delta.json` and
`cumulative-release-scope.json` beneath its audit root plus the audit result. In
`index` and `commit` modes it accepts both expected records, first verifies both
required expected-record SHA-256 arguments, recomputes the staged or commit sets
and hashes, and requires exact byte/entry equality. Worktree mode forbids all
four expected-record arguments. It
rejects ignored/untracked extras, missing paths, symlink/reparse/hard-link
members, status/index drift, unexpected base/target identities, output
preexistence, or a repository output path. All Git/native calls use the same
checked subprocess adapter. Tests use injected processes and disposable tiny
repositories; none resolves a proposed6 or historical evidence root.
Scope `closure` requires the reviewed closure-parent identity and the exact
three fixed closure paths plus the complete dynamic approved6 regular-file
inventory. Scope `final-docs` requires target parent equal the already reviewed
closure commit, permits exactly the one completion-plan blob in the commit
delta, and derives cumulative scope as the closure record plus that blob. The
expected parent is mandatory in every mode and is rechecked around every Git
projection.

Finally, add RED parser, pure-validation, and injected-launcher tests for the
exact Task 14 execution interface before it can ever be used with a credential:

```text
run_complete_suite_campaign.py execute
  --campaign tests/skills/complete-suite-campaign.yaml
  --approved-campaign-sha256 <64 lowercase hex>
  --provider-approval-record <absolute D:\tmp path>

  --expected-approval-envelope-sha256 <64 lowercase hex>
  --credential-transport-version complete-suite-provider-credential-pipe-v1
  --provider-credential-environment OPENAI_API_KEY
```

Expose a closed `validate_provider_execution_authorization` helper that receives
captured campaign, approval-envelope, provider-prompt, and provider-record
bytes; a no-follow captured `ProviderAttemptReservation`; and an immutable
`ProviderExecutionPreclaimState` containing the no-follow marker/terminal/raw/
retained absence captures plus their nearest-existing-parent identities. It
receives every expected hash plus the exact credential transport version/name
and returns the detached `ProviderExecutionAuthorization` with the exact
ordered canonical bytes defined above. It requires the atomic
`approved_not_started` transition, the stored draft/envelope/review bindings,
canonical prompt and provider-record bytes, the v2 capture/authentication labels,
exact response reconstruction/hash, exact campaign ID/count/concurrency/roots,
zero starts, the exact campaign-bound reservation present, execute-consumption/
terminal/raw/retained paths absent, one-shot/no-retry, and the literal
`complete-suite-provider-credential-pipe-v1`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` pair. Its fresh
post-GO preclaim bytes must hash identically to the broker-retained pre-ACK
snapshot before marker or claim.
This helper is Task 10 role code: the bootstrap cannot import or call it before
ACK. The restricted `root_role_entrypoint` target for `execute` calls it exactly
once immediately after that target's authenticated GO and role import, freshly
reopening every input rather than trusting the
`ExecutePreAckReceipt`, and only its detached return may be passed to
`consume_provider_execute`. Thus the Task 9 pre-ACK check and Task 10 post-GO
authorization are distinct validators on distinct sides of the import gate.
Changed bytes, extra arguments, an alternate credential name, an already-used
approval, stale campaign, missing/changed reservation, terminal/root presence,
execute-consumption presence, or counter drift must stop before execute-marker
or raw-root mutation, environment materialization, or launcher invocation. Successful tests
use only a synthetic credential and injected inert launcher beneath a pytest
temporary root; no test may resolve the real proposed6 root or make a socket
connection.

The subsequent claimed execution reopens the one campaign-bound candidate-input
aggregate and uses this exact no-process API; it accepts no independently
supplied executable or manifest path:

```text
reopen_campaign_codex_client_identity(
    approved: ApprovedCampaign,
    candidate_inputs_record: CapturedLaunchInput,
) -> FrozenCodexClientIdentity
```

It requires the aggregate record path/identity/size/hash embedded in `approved`,
derives the constituent client-preflight record and both package manifests from
that aggregate, calls `validate_frozen_codex_client_identity`, and rechecks the
aggregate plus executable/package identities around every read. It returns the
exact native executable only after the label is process-free proven as
`codex-cli 0.149.0`. There is no `version_factory`, environment/PATH discovery,
`codex --version`, shim, Node, or package-manager callback.

`authorize-provider` is also the sole producer of a content-authenticated attempt
reservation. After validating the exact user approval and before publishing the
`approved_not_started` campaign transition, it atomically no-replace writes and
fsyncs `provider-attempt-consumption.json` in the fresh executor-created
approval directory that contains the provider-approval record, using the closed
`complete-suite-provider-attempt-consumption-v1` schema. The reservation binds
the campaign ID, prompt/draft/envelope/provider-approval hashes, exact future
raw/retained paths, 24 runs, four-worker maximum, zero starts, and
`retry_allowed:false`, plus the exact
`complete-suite-provider-credential-pipe-v1` transport and `OPENAI_API_KEY`
name; it contains no credential or private error text. The
campaign transition binds its SHA-256. If reservation publication fails, the
authorization command does not report success or mutate the campaign, and that
user response is not silently reused: a later attempt requires a newly presented
record and a new explicit approval. Once the reservation exists, the provider
approval is durably consumed even if execution is never entered. The
reservation is not itself evidence that one `execute` invocation already
entered; the separate execute-consumption marker below supplies that
distinction.

After that content-authenticated reservation-backed authorization succeeds, the
pre-ACK root bootstrap performs only pure validation of the authorization/reservation
and absence of execute marker, terminal, raw root, and claim. It writes none of
them. After the root ACK/GO and the restricted target's own ACK/GO, and still
before reading the credential, materializing an environment, preparing a case,
or starting any native/client/provider descendant or socket, the imported
execute target alone crosses the execute-consumption and raw-root claim
boundaries:

The authenticated root Python bootstrap and its one restricted execute target
are already running at this point and are recorded in the process manifest.
Every zero-launch or zero-provider-process statement in this execution lifecycle
means no native leaf, Codex client, provider process, or additional target beyond
those two fixed infrastructure processes; it does not claim that the broker or
execute target is absent.

```text
consume_provider_execute(
    authorization: ProviderExecutionAuthorization,

claim_provider_attempt(

    *,

SealableClaimedCampaignPreparationEvidence = (

seal_reserved_zero_run_failure(
    reservation: ProviderAttemptReservation,
    execution: ProviderExecuteConsumption | None,
    *,
    code: Literal[
        "CAMPAIGN_AUTHORIZATION_TRANSITION_FAILED",
        "CAMPAIGN_AUTHORIZATION_COMMIT_FAILED",
        "CAMPAIGN_EXECUTE_CONSUMPTION_FAILED",
        "CAMPAIGN_ATTEMPT_CLAIM_FAILED",
    ],
) -> Path

capture_claimed_campaign_preparation_evidence(

prepare_claimed_campaign(
```
