```text
) -> ClaimedCampaignPreparationResult

seal_zero_run_failure(
    claim: ProviderAttemptClaim,
    *,
    claim_only_evidence: ClaimedCampaignPreparationEvidence,
    preparation: SealableClaimedCampaignPreparationEvidence,
    transport: SealableCredentialTransport,
    code: Literal[
        "CAMPAIGN_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE",
        "CAMPAIGN_SECRET_ISOLATION_FAILED",
        "CAMPAIGN_LAUNCH_PREFLIGHT_FAILED",
        "CAMPAIGN_LAUNCH_MATERIALIZATION_FAILED",
        "CAMPAIGN_PREPARATION_FAILED",
    ],
) -> Path
```

Immediately after the target's authenticated GO and execute-role import, and before
credential access, environment materialization, case preparation, or any
native/client/provider descendant or socket, that restricted target calls
`consume_provider_execute` exactly once. No root bootstrap, host helper, other
target, caller, or retry path may call it. The function
exclusively no-replace writes
and fsyncs canonical `provider-execute-consumption.json` beside the reservation.
Its closed `complete-suite-provider-execute-consumption-v1` record binds the
exact approved-campaign, draft, approval-envelope, provider-approval, and
reservation hashes; campaign ID; future raw/retained paths; 24 runs; four-worker
maximum; zero starts/completions; `retry_allowed:false`; and the exact
`complete-suite-provider-credential-pipe-v1`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` pair. It contains no
credential, timestamp, random value, or private error text. It reopens and
revalidates the record, reservation, parent identities, campaign bytes, and
marker-parent membership before returning immutable byte-backed evidence. Only
the invocation whose exclusive create and reopen both succeed may continue. An
invocation that observes the marker already present rejects without treating
identical bytes as an idempotent retry. Thus a process exit after marker
publication leaves a durable consumed-execute fact and every later invocation
rejects before raw-root work.

Inject marker failpoints before CreateNew, after CreateNew but before fsync,
after fsync but before reopen, and during final parent/membership recapture. On
any returned publication exception, recapture the marker no-follow. If it is the
exact completely published record, classify the attempt consumed but do not
continue from the ambiguous callback; publish the safe reservation-terminal
outcome below. If it is proven stably absent, publish terminal code
`CAMPAIGN_EXECUTE_CONSUMPTION_FAILED`. An indeterminate, partial, replaced, or
unexpected present marker is `invalid_consumed_attempt`; perform no repair or
raw-root write. Process-termination tests kill the injected child immediately
after successful marker publication and prove a fresh `execute` rejects with
zero raw-root change and zero descendant-process/socket/provider creation. The reviewed command defines
successful exclusive marker publication as its durable execute-entry boundary;
validation failures before that boundary mutate nothing and cannot be
misreported as an entered attempt.

`claim_provider_attempt` first revalidates the no-follow reservation and execute-
consumption paths, identities, exact bytes/hashes, parent identities, and
campaign binding, then publishes the approved raw root exactly once with an
atomic no-replace transition and a canonical, fsynced
`provider-attempt.json` using the closed
`complete-suite-provider-attempt-v1` schema. The claim binds campaign ID,
approved campaign/draft/envelope/provider-approval hashes, raw-root identity,
24 authorized runs, four-worker maximum, zero starts/completions, and
`retry_allowed:false`, plus the exact
`complete-suite-provider-credential-pipe-v1`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` pair; it contains
no credential, clock-derived decision, or
private error text. Both reservation and execute-consumption SHA-256 values are
copied into the claim.

The same restricted execute target then calls `claim_provider_attempt` exactly
once; no pre-GO code, root bootstrap, host helper, other target, or retry path
owns that transition. After the marker, root, and claim are durably published
and reopened, the target immediately calls
`capture_claimed_campaign_preparation_evidence` once while holding the claim/root
no-follow identities. That producer authenticates the canonical claim bytes,
requires claim-only membership, serializes and reopens the exact immutable
`ClaimedCampaignPreparationEvidence` bytes, and returns the sole original in-
memory claim-only object whose provenance may be used by any later sealer. Its
state is permanently `claim-only`, its creation ledger is empty, and its
failure stage is null. No caller may mutate, copy, reconstruct, deserialize, or
replace it. The target then validates the frozen client identity. A failure
before calling `prepare_claimed_campaign` creates only the private typed
`ClaimedCampaignPreparationNotStartedEvidence` through the execute state
machine; that object holds the exact original by reference, binds its canonical
SHA-256 plus the same claim/root/manifest identities, and has
`successor_evidence:null`. It does not fabricate a post-preparation successor.
On the preparation path, the target passes the exact original object into
`prepare_claimed_campaign`, receives a distinct immutable successor in the
result, and verifies the canonical
`credential-pipe-lifecycle.json` and `credential-lifecycle.json` destinations
are absent beneath the prepared skeleton.
Only then does it send exactly one canonical secret-free
`ExecuteClaimCapability` as its sole outstanding broker request. It has no
secret-pipe constructor, host-status writer,
credential lookup, spawn-environment materializer, or client constructor. The
trusted root-broker independently validates the capability with
`validate_execute_claim_capability_stdlib`, reopens every bound fact, creates the
nonce-bound credential-data and host-status pipe pair, and emits canonical
`ExecuteClaimReady` as the bounded
authenticated host-facing `claim-ready` status frame. Credential lookup and
transfer remain forbidden until the pipe peers validate one another, the root
emits canonical `ExecuteCredentialPeerAccepted`, and the host independently
reopens and validates all facts named by both frames. Failure before the target
GO writes nothing; failure
after marker/claim follows only the already defined consumed terminal or
invalid-attempt branches.

After the execute marker and raw-root claim plus the exact claim-only preparation
evidence are durably authenticated, but before capability publication,
credential access, or any native/client/provider child or socket start, the
execute target calls
`reopen_campaign_codex_client_identity`. A mismatch is the bounded
`CAMPAIGN_LAUNCH_PREFLIGHT_FAILED` zero-run outcome because the approval and
execute attempt are already consumed; that sealer call receives the exact
claim-only producer object, the exact non-reconstructed not-started evidence,
and the private capability-not-sent token from this execute state machine. On
success, it places only the returned
identity digest and launch-template digest in `ExecuteClaimCapability`; the
broker derives and reopens the actual paths from its authenticated descriptor.
Never pass an arbitrary executable path or call the legacy `_plain_executable`
plus `_codex_version` sequence.

After any raw-root/claim publication exception, recapture both paths no-follow.
Continue only if the exact root/claim were completely published and revalidate;
seal the execute-consumed zero-run branch only if both are proven stably absent
and the exact execute-consumption marker still revalidates. An indeterminate,
partial, replaced, or unexpected present path is `invalid_consumed_attempt` and
permits no further write. If both remain absent while the reservation and marker
still revalidate, `seal_reserved_zero_run_failure` atomically no-replace
publishes `provider-attempt-terminal.json` beside them with both hashes,
`runs_authorized:24`, `runs_started:0`, `runs_completed:0`, code
`CAMPAIGN_ATTEMPT_CLAIM_FAILED`, status `reserved_zero_run_failure`, and
`retry_allowed:false`, plus `credential_pipe_lifecycle_sha256:null` and
`credential_lifecycle_sha256:null`. It writes
nowhere beneath the uncreated raw root and
reopens/verifies the terminal record. If reservation/marker ancestry, identity,
or bytes drift, or terminal publication itself fails, stop with host-only
`CAMPAIGN_ATTEMPT_RESERVATION_INTEGRITY_FAILED`, perform no repair or retry, and
leave the existing content-authenticated consumption facts untouched.

The same reservation sealer closes the authorization-transition window. If the
reservation is validly published but the atomic campaign transition fails
before or after replace/reopen, `authorize-provider` proves raw/retained roots
absent and publishes terminal code
`CAMPAIGN_AUTHORIZATION_TRANSITION_FAILED`. If it cannot safely publish that
terminal, the reservation alone remains the consumed/no-retry fact and the
outcome is `invalid_consumed_attempt`. A failure before any reservation target
becomes visible mutates neither campaign nor roots and publishes no terminal;
the earlier response is not automatically reused and a new explicit approval is
required. RED failpoints cover before CreateNew, a partial/invalid reservation,
valid reservation before campaign replace, after replace before reopen, and
final reopen/hash failure.

It also closes the narrower Task 14 post-transition/pre-execute commit window.
After `authorize-provider` has returned success, any exact campaign-delta,
stage, commit, root-absence, reservation, or clean-status assertion failure is
caught before `execute`. The reviewed
`close-provider-authorization-failure` command may then publish only code
`CAMPAIGN_AUTHORIZATION_COMMIT_FAILED` while the approved campaign,
authorization reservation, approval bytes, sibling membership, and all four
absence facts still revalidate. Otherwise it writes nothing and the
content-authenticated reservation remains an `invalid_consumed_attempt`. No
failure in this window
permits a second authorization or execution attempt.

Campaign 6 must never call the legacy `prepare_approved_campaign` path that
creates the raw root. `prepare_claimed_campaign` opens the already claimed root
no-follow, requires the same root identity and exact canonical claim bytes/hash,
requires its initial membership to contain only `provider-attempt.json`, and
rechecks the nearest existing ancestor and root identity around every callback.
It creates only the missing campaign child directories/files under that bound
root, using the existing preparation logic after its root-creation boundary.
It returns `ClaimedCampaignPreparationResult`, never a bare path and never an
untyped exception after the claim boundary. Before each create it selects the
next literal manifest member. While the returned no-follow handle remains open,
it captures that member's relative path, kind, identity, and fixed-content hash
and appends exactly one immutable `PreparedMemberEvidence`; only then may it
close the handle or start the next create. It catches every preparation error,
performs one final no-follow root/membership recapture, and returns a closed
failure result without exception text. A member visible without a completed
ledger entry, an identity/hash mismatch, or inability to perform that recapture
sets `successor_evidence.state="untrusted"`. An exact strict subset sets
`partial`; only an unchanged original claim-only membership with no visible
prepared member and an empty creation ledger sets `claim-only`, and only the
complete fixed manifest with both lifecycle destinations absent sets
`complete`.
Campaign 6 calls it exactly once after frozen-client validation and before
`ExecuteClaimCapability`, with a freshly built secret-free base environment and
the exact non-reconstructed claim-only evidence returned immediately after the
claim. The preparation function requires object identity, canonical bytes/hash,
claim/root identities, and initial membership to match that producer return
before its first create. Every return contains a newly constructed
`ClaimedCampaignPostPreparationEvidence` that is not the original object and
whose private `original_claim_only_evidence` reference must be that original by
`is`. Its canonical bytes bind the original evidence SHA-256, claim SHA-256,
root identity, expected-manifest SHA-256, completed/public-code pair, exact
state, creation ledger, observed-membership SHA-256, and failure stage; the
private original-object reference plus wrapper-only canonical bytes/hash fields
are not serialized. The function strictly encodes, hashes, reparses, and
revalidates those canonical bytes before returning the sole non-reconstructed
successor object. `ClaimedCampaignPreparationResult.completed` and
`.public_code` must exactly equal the successor's corresponding
`preparation_completed` and `preparation_public_code` fields. The original
claim-only object's fields, canonical bytes, and hash remain byte-for-byte
unchanged.
Only a result with `completed:true`, `public_code:null`, matching successor
`preparation_completed:true`/`preparation_public_code:null`, and successor state `complete`
may publish that capability. The resulting closed skeleton includes the exact parent for, but neither
`credential-pipe-lifecycle.json` nor `credential-lifecycle.json`; the root-
broker independently reopens that prepared identity/membership and both absent
slots before creating the credential pipe.
The claim SHA-256 is copied into every run declaration and later campaign
ledger/completion/inventory/seal. A second root-creation attempt, extra initial
member, swapped root/claim, changed identity, reparse/hard-link transition, or
claim/hash mismatch fails before any descendant-process/socket/provider start. Historical
campaigns retain their current absent-root preparation path byte-for-byte.

Every failure after the claim and before the first provider `CreateProcessW`
success is caught at this boundary and classified before any terminal write.
`seal_zero_run_failure` is callable only with the exact producer-returned
original `claim_only_evidence`, one exact non-reconstructed member of
`SealableClaimedCampaignPreparationEvidence`, and one closed
`SealableCredentialTransport`. Every post-claim path retains and passes the
original separately. Missing, copied, deserialized, reconstructed, replaced, or
cross-attempt original, not-started, or successor objects are not sealer inputs.
The legal preparation combinations are closed:

- before `prepare_claimed_campaign` is entered, the preparation argument is the
  exact internally issued `ClaimedCampaignPreparationNotStartedEvidence`; its
  private original reference is the separately supplied original by `is`, its
  original hash plus claim/root/manifest identities match, and
  `successor_evidence` is exactly null. No successor may exist or be fabricated;
  the transport is `NoCapabilityRequestBeforeReadiness`;
- once `prepare_claimed_campaign` is entered, not-started evidence is illegal
  and the exact returned `ClaimedCampaignPostPreparationEvidence` is required.
  A failed result may seal only code `CAMPAIGN_PREPARATION_FAILED`, with
  `preparation_completed:false`, the matching public code, a no-capability
  transport, and either exact safe `claim-only` state when no prepared member
  became visible and the ledger is empty, or exact `complete` state when the
  full fixed manifest and both absent lifecycle slots were proven. Any other
  completed/public-code/state combination is `invalid_consumed_attempt`;
- a successful result requires `preparation_completed:true`, null public code,
  and exact `complete` state. That complete successor is required on every
  later capability, pre-readiness, readiness, credential-transport, and other
  post-preparation zero-run path. The original remains the separate unchanged
  claim-only object; a successful path with no successor or with a claim-only
  successor is invalid; and
- `partial` or `untrusted` successor state is always
  `invalid_consumed_attempt`, even when every visible member has a ledger entry.

Before readiness there are exactly two disjoint permitted inputs. A failure
before the capability send requires `NoCapabilityRequestBeforeReadiness`, the
private token from that exact execute state-machine instance, an exact null
capability hash, and both lifecycle slots reopened absent. A failure after the
capability send requires `AuthenticatedPreReadinessBrokerFailureTransport`, the
exact authenticated canonical broker response bytes/hash for that capability,
`readiness_emitted:false`, and four null lifecycle projections. Both variants
require zero lookup/transfer/accept counts and no provider process. A sent
capability with missing, synthesized, malformed, or cross-attempt response
evidence is `invalid_consumed_attempt`.
After readiness, the only permitted transport input is
`AuthenticatedCredentialTransport`: the status/data protocols are terminal with
zero outstanding I/O, its nested response evidence carries both canonical
lifecycle objects and hashes, and its nested persistence evidence proves the
target persisted them create-new in pipe-then-credential order and both exact
bytes reopened under the captured prepared root before construction.
An orderly authorization, lookup, unavailable-credential, or transfer failure
after readiness may therefore seal only after that complete authenticated pair
exists. Missing/malformed/mismatched host status; impossible counter/progress;
peer or binding failure; unretired I/O; deadline termination; partial/mismatched
lifecycle publication; response authentication failure; pre-readiness lifecycle
presence; or any provider `CreateProcessW` success is
`invalid_consumed_attempt` and must not call this sealer.

For each permitted variant, the sealer reopens the root and claim no-follow,
requires their captured identities, exact canonical claim bytes/hash, ancestry,
and the evidence-defined membership. It requires the separately supplied
original to be the producer-returned in-memory object, recomputes and reparses
its unchanged canonical claim-only bytes/hash, and revalidates its empty ledger,
claim/root/manifest bindings, and original membership. It then requires the
not-started or successor object's private original reference to be that same
object by `is`, recomputes and reparses that object's canonical bytes/hash, and
revalidates every duplicated original hash, claim/root/manifest identity,
result-state field, ledger entry, membership, and failure stage. Equality of
values does not substitute for either object-identity check. For an
authenticated post-readiness transport it reparses
`response_evidence.authenticated_response_canonical_bytes`, recomputes its hash,
validates the complete persistence-evidence object, reopens the exact
`credential-pipe-lifecycle.json` and `credential-lifecycle.json` bytes, and
requires byte-for-byte equality and the host-status-to-pipe-to-credential hash
DAG; it never accepts independent lifecycle hash arguments. It then writes/
fsyncs the canonical campaign ledger, completion, inventory, seal, and
`COMPLETED` marker with `runs_authorized:24`, `runs_started:0`,
`runs_completed:0`, `sealed_zero_run_failure`, `retry_allowed:false`, and the
variant's exact null-or-paired projections, and reopens every byte. It invokes no
external callback and no provider, network, process-construction, or lookup API.
The target terminal is emitted only after sealing and repeats the projections;
the root's later final process record independently embeds the same objects, so
the ownership graph is acyclic.

If root/claim identity, bytes, ancestry, evidence, or membership does not match,
emit only host-side code `CAMPAIGN_CLAIM_INTEGRITY_FAILED`, stop without any
further write beneath that path, and do not call the zero-run sealer. The
approval remains consumed and the path is `invalid_consumed_attempt`, never
`sealed_zero_run_failure`. Neither branch stores an exception type/message or
credential value. Once any provider `CreateProcessW` has succeeded, the ordinary
immutable started-run failure path applies and can never be relabeled zero-run.

The command runs `complete_suite_preparation.capture_runtime_wheelhouse` twice
and requires the same seven distributions, filenames, sizes, hashes,
tree/inventory digests,
root identity, membership, and canonical manifest bytes, with no directory,
extra entry, reparse point, symlink, or link count other than one. Set every
wheel's Windows `IsReadOnly` flag, prove a write-open fails, and recapture again.
It retains the canonical manifest only in the aggregate record, never inside
the wheelhouse. It offline-smokes the wheelhouse into a fresh attempt-owned
install root. With repository source removed from `sys.path`, require all seven
distributions to resolve below that target, CLI version/help and Rin validation to pass, and
the target inventory to remain unchanged. Re-capture the wheelhouse a final
time. Any mismatch, network attempt, or write makes Campaign 6 preparation fail.

It resolves the installed Codex data home only from the explicit argument at
this preapproval discovery boundary and freezes the two validator scripts
through Task 9's reviewed helper. The validator record is canonical and
contains exactly the two source-relative locators, pinned wheel/runtime, and D:
bundle facts defined in Task 10, without the Codex-home/user-profile path.
Revalidate the bundle twice, require exact source/bundle byte equality and no
network/repository write, then make both scripts and every runtime file
read-only and revalidate once more. The campaign later binds the wheel,
runtime, bundle manifests, and every file identity; it never rediscovers a
validator or dependency from environment state. It then freezes the exact final
installed-client proof through Task 9's reviewed producer, not pytest output or
an inline serializer.

## Plan self-review checklist

Before implementation begins, verify:

- [ ] Every approved design section 1 through 14 maps to at least one task.
- [ ] Approved5 remains immutable and explicitly legacy-routed.
- [ ] The exact 12 cases and 24-run matrix cannot drift silently.
- [ ] Syntax decoding and operation authorization are separate modules.
- [ ] Raw and retained plans are decoded independently and normalized.
- [ ] Output binding is ordered, bounded, duplicate-key-safe, and capture-bound.
- [ ] Every state-changing client item is lifecycle-classified; the symmetric
  optional file-change policies, aggregate transitions, content/resource bounds,
  and complete filesystem projection are evidence-bound.
- [ ] Integrity failure makes all declared assertions false before inversion.
- [ ] Shell/client/meta inputs are frozen without arbitrary user-profile reads.
- [ ] Git/Node leaves and autocrlf materialization are identity-bound and prove
  zero native descendants; `git clone` is absent from every executable path.
- [ ] Guarded children use atomic Job-list creation, exact standard/IPC handles,
  and one deadline; Codex-owned descendants use the separately disclosed client
  TCB, exact client-limit table, and after-creation Job reconciliation.
- [ ] Every registered Windows constructor is dominated by
  `complete-suite-windows-native-vector-v1`, accepts at most 30,000 UTF-16 units
  including its terminal NUL, and binds the recomputed unit count/UTF-16LE hash;
  exact-at/one-over and per-site bypass mutants are covered.
- [ ] Every Codex process has a truthful evaluation envelope before spawn;
  metadata never bypasses cybersecurity review or widens agent-shell policy.
- [ ] Every host collaboration review has a phase/type-closed envelope before
  spawn, an exact content-complete phase bundle, an exact captured result, and a
  fresh mechanical audit; host calls never
  increment or substitute for the fixed 4 + 4 + 24 local Windows client count.
- [ ] The host-review bundle evidence oracle is the literal 2/7/9-row
  candidate/closure/final-docs table: exact continuous two-digit ordinals,
  roles, fixed leaves, source artifacts, phase membership, `100644` modes,
  bytes/hashes, and order, with byte-identical cross-process output for
  identical inputs and no caller-selected or discovered evidence source.
- [ ] Every quality/security host-review audit captures and authenticates the
  retained same-phase specification PASS result path/identity/size/bytes/hash;
  every specification audit records explicit null and rejects predecessor input.
- [ ] Every operator and host-review artifact call has a distinct pinned chain:
  one fresh `tty:true` session with its console-host companion, one outer
  `exec_command` PowerShell bootstrap with `login:false`, exactly one framed
  nonempty `write_stdin` plus only the bounded same-session empty polls needed to
  observe terminal exit, then exactly one direct Python writer with exact
  `-I -S -B -X utf8` argv; PowerShell exe/dll, launcher, and Python executable/
  runtime/helper identities are exact, receipt -> trust record -> manifest
  launcher/helper derivation is cross-checked, and the request is closed framed
  data outside argv. Pre-entry outer environment/CLR activity is explicitly in the
  stable-host TCB; the first plan statement performs only the post-start names-
  family drift check and binds its zero-count marker. The exact two-name child
  environment is checked outside and inside, with no inherited value transferred
  and no runtime type, PowerShell cmdlet, module, profile, PATH, or cache used.
- [ ] Artifact and audit publication re-resolve canonical `D:\tmp`, deny delete
  sharing on retained directory handles, retain pair predecessors with no write/
  delete sharing, and reject handle-derived oversize before allocation.
- [ ] Invalid or missing deletion parameters return the stable argument error
  before callbacks and leave identities, membership, and bytes unchanged.
- [ ] Task 11 audits only its authenticated detached provisional tree, and the
  reviewed closure commit passes the executable `closure-reviewed` successor
  gate before any docs-only completion edit.
- [ ] Every new file has an explicit LF checkout rule.
- [ ] Every behavior change has a named RED and GREEN command.
- [ ] Every implementation slice ends in a focused commit.
- [ ] Provider execution and evidence import are distinct explicit stop gates.
- [ ] No step modifies historical evidence, retries a campaign, or claims
  success from synthetic data.

## Completion boundary for the authorized implementation phase

The presently authorized phase ends when Task 13 has produced a clean,
reviewed, fresh-checkout-reproducible proposed6 draft and exact approval
envelope with the proposed6 raw and retained roots absent and zero provider
starts. The selected read-only Task 12 candidate-input attempt and aggregate
record are already frozen and approval-bound at this point; all obsolete
attempts remain inert and unreferenced. Tasks 14
through 16 are retained here as the exact continuation runbook, but their
external effects remain gated by the approved design's hash-bound
authorizations.
